He looked at me, greeted me, and gave me good tidings. I said: 'How long have you been standing over Hell?' He said: 'Since I was created until now, and so it will be until the Hour arrives.' I said: 'O Jibril, I wish to see a glimpse of the Fire.' He ordered it, and it did so. A blazing, black flame came forth, with murky, dark smoke, which filled the horizons. I saw a great terror and a dreadful matter, which I am unable to describe to you. I fainted and nearly lost my life. Jibril embraced me and commanded that the Fire be returned, and it was returned."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We passed on and came to many angels whose number none can count except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Some of them had faces between their shoulders and faces on their chests, and every face had mouths and tongues. They praised Allah and glorified Him with those tongues. I saw among their bodies, their forms and their worship, a tremendous wonder. We then passed on, and there was a man of perfect creation, lacking nothing of the creation of human beings. On his right was a door from which a good fragrance came forth, and on his left was a door from which a foul odor came forth. When he looked at the door on his right, he laughed; when he looked at the door on his left, he wept in sorrow. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this, and what are these two doors?' He said: 'This is your father Adam (peace be upon him). The door on his right is the gate of Paradise. When he looks at those of his descendants who enter Paradise, he laughs and rejoices. The door on his left is the gate of Hell. When he looks at those of his descendants who enter Hell, he weeps and grieves.'

Then we ascended to the second heaven, and Jibril (peace be upon him) asked for entry. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming.' We entered and saw two youths. I said: 'O Jibril, who are these two youths?' He said: 'These are Isa and Yahya, cousins on the mother's side.'

Then I ascended to the third heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' We entered and saw a man who was endowed above people with beauty, like the finest moon on the night of the full moon above the other stars. I said: 'Who is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is your brother Yusuf (peace be upon him).'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then I was taken up to the fourth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' We entered and saw a man in a [kadha] state. I said: 'Who is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is Idris, whom Allah raised to a lofty place,' and he was leaning his back against the registers of the creatures, in which their affairs are recorded.

Then I was taken up to the fifth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.'

Then we entered and saw a man sitting, around whom were people he was recounting to. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this, and who are those around him?' He said: 'This is Harun, the beloved [al-Muhabbab], and those around him are the Children of Israel.'"

"Then we ascended to the sixth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' Then we entered and saw a man sitting. We passed by him, and the man wept. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this?' He said: 'This is Musa.' I said: 'Why is he weeping?' He said: 'The Children of Israel claim that I am the most honored of the children of Adam before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This man is a man of the children of Adam, and he has been left behind by me in his worldly life, while I am in my afterlife. If it were only himself, I would not mind, but with every prophet there is his community.'"

He said: "Then I was taken up to the seventh heaven, and he asked for entry. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' Then we entered and saw a man [grey-haired] sitting on a chair at the gate of Paradise. Around him were people sitting with [white] faces like sheets of paper, and other people in whose complexions there was something [...] [[A blank in the manuscript. In Tafsir al-Tabari (15/15) the speech is continuous, and in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/71) there is an addition: 'Isa, i.e. Abu Ja'far al-Razi, said: I heard him say once: black faces.']]

Those in whose complexions there was something stood up, entered a river, bathed in it, and came out, and some of the something had left their complexions. Then they entered another river, bathed in it, and came out, and it had completely left their complexions, which became like the complexions of their companions. They came and sat beside their companions. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this grey-haired man, who are these people, and what are these rivers?' He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the first to turn grey upon the earth. As for these white-faced people, they are a people who have not mixed their faith with wrongdoing. As for those who had something in their complexions, they are a people who mixed righteous deeds with others that were evil, then repented, and Allah accepted their repentance. As for the three rivers: the first is the mercy of Allah, the second is the blessing of Allah, and the third is "their Lord gave them a pure drink." He said: Then I found Ibrahim leaning against a house, and I asked Jibril. He said: This is the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and when they leave it they never return to it again.'

He said: 'Then Jibril brought me until we reached the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). There I saw a tree whose single leaf covered the world with what it contains, and its fruit was like the jars of Hajar. Four rivers emerged from its root: two apparent and two hidden. I asked Jibril about them. He said: "As for the two hidden ones, they are in Paradise. As for the two apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates." Also from its root come "rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste does not alter, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey." It lies at the edge of the seventh heaven; Paradise, its roots and its branches are beneath the Throne.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reached the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I knew that it was the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I knew its leaves and its fruit. There covered it of the light of Allah what covered it, and the angels covered it like locusts of gold out of fear of Allah, Exalted is He. When what covered it covered it, it transformed until no one could prevent it. He said: There are angels in it whose number none knows except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the station of Jibril is in its midst. When I reached it, Jibril said to me: 'Go forward!' I said: 'Forward of whom? You go forward, O Muhammad, for you are more honored by Allah than I am.' I went forward, with Jibril following my steps, until he brought me to a veil of gold brocade, and he shook the veil. It said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'I am Jibril, and with me is Muhammad.' The angel said: 'Allah is greater.' He extended his hand from beneath the veil, lifted me up, and left Jibril behind. I said to him: 'Where are you taking me?' He said: 'O Muhammad, "There is none of us but has a known station." This is the limit of the creatures. I was only permitted to approach the veil out of respect for you and because of your majesty.'"

He said: "Then the angel carried me, faster than the blink of an eye, to a veil of pearls, and he shook the veil. The angel said from behind the veil: 'Who is this?' He said: 'I am the keeper of the gold brocade, and with me is Muhammad, the Messenger of the Arabs.' The angel said: 'Allah is greater,' and extended his hand from beneath the veil, lifted me up, and placed me before Him. I continued thus from veil to veil until they had brought me past seventy veils. The thickness of each veil was a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between one veil and the next was a five-hundred-year journey. Then a green canopy was lowered for me, whose light overcame the light of the sun, and my sight was dazzled. I was placed upon that canopy, and it carried me until it brought me to the Throne. When I saw the Throne, everything near the Throne became clear. Allah brought me close to the support of the Throne, and a drop from the Throne descended and settled upon my tongue. No one who has tasted anything has ever tasted anything sweeter than it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed me by it of the news of the first and the last. Allah loosed my tongue, which had been stilled by awe of the Most Merciful. I said: 'All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah.' Allah, Exalted is He, said: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' I said: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.' He said: 'O Muhammad, do you know about what the Exalted Assembly disputed?' I said: 'You, O Lord, know best about that and about everything, and You are the Knower of the unseen.' He said: 'They disputed about the ranks and the good deeds. Do you know, O Muhammad, what the ranks and the good deeds are?' I said: 'You know best, O Lord.' He said: 'The ranks are completing the ablution in difficult conditions, walking on foot to congregations, and waiting for prayers after prayers. The good deeds are spreading peace, feeding food, and performing the night prayer while people sleep.' Then He said: 'O Muhammad, "The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord"?' I said: 'Yes, O Lord.' He said: 'And the believers?' I said: '"Each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers; we make no distinction between any of His messengers," as the Jews and Christians made distinctions.' He said: 'What did they say?' I said: '"We hear and we obey." ' He said: 'You have spoken truly; ask and you will be given.' I said: '"Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return."' He said: 'I have forgiven you and your community. Ask and you will be given.' I said: '"Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err."' He said: 'I have lifted the error and forgetfulness from you and your community, and what they are compelled to.' I said: '"Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear."' He said: 'I have done that for you and your community.' I said: '"Our Lord, pardon us from being swallowed up by the earth, forgive us from being struck down by a calamity, and have mercy on us from being transformed. You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelieving people."' He said: 'I have done that for you and your community.' Then it was said to me: 'Ask.'

I said: 'O Lord, You took Ibrahim as a friend, You spoke to Musa directly, You raised Idris to a lofty place, You gave Sulayman a great kingdom, and You gave Dawud the Psalms. What then is mine, O Lord?' My Lord said: 'O Muhammad, I have taken you as a friend as I took Ibrahim as a friend, and I have spoken to you as I spoke to Musa directly. I have given you the Opening of the Book and the final verses of al-Baqarah, which were among the treasures of the Throne, and I have not given them to any prophet before you. I have sent you to the people of the earth, all of them, white and black, humankind and jinn, and I did not send any prophet to all of them before you. I have made the entire earth, its land and its sea, pure and a place of prostration for you and your community. I have fed you and your community from the spoils, and I did not feed any community before them. I have aided you with terror against your enemy from a distance of a month's journey. I have sent down to you the chief of all the books and its guardian, "a Qur'an We have divided." I have raised your remembrance, so you are remembered whenever I am remembered in the laws of My religion. I have given you in place of the Torah the oft-repeated (al-mathani), in place of the Gospel the manifest, and in place of the Psalms the Hawamim. I have favored you with the detailed (al-mufassal), I have expanded your breast, I have removed your burden, and I have made your community "the best community brought forth for humankind," and I have made them "a middle nation," and I have made them the first, while they are the last. So take what I have given you, and be among the thankful.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then He entrusted me, after that, with a covenant concerning matters which I was not permitted to tell you. Then fifty prayers were enjoined upon me and my community each day and night. When He had testified to me of His covenant and left me in His presence for as long as He willed, He said to me: 'Return to your people and convey My message to them.' The green canopy on which I had been carried took me, lowering and raising me, until it swept me down to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. There I saw Jibril (peace be upon him) behind me with my heart, just as I saw him in front of me with my eyes. Jibril said to me: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, for you are the best of Allah's creation and His chosen one among the prophets. May Allah greet you with what He has not greeted anyone of His creation, neither a near angel nor a sent prophet. He has placed you in a station that none of the people of the heavens and the earth has reached. May Allah congratulate you on His honor and on the preeminent station and the surpassing dignity He has bestowed upon you. So take it and give thanks, for Allah is a Bestower who loves the thankful.'"

I praised God for that. Then Jibril said to me: "Go, O Muhammad, to Paradise, so that I may show you what is prepared for you in it, so that you may grow in asceticism in this world to match your asceticism, and in desire for the Hereafter to match your desire." So we set off, descending swiftly, faster than an arrow and the wind, until by God's permission we reached Paradise. My soul was calmed, and my heart returned to me. I began to ask Jibril about what I had seen in Paradise of seas, fire, light and other things, and he said:

"Glory be to God! Those are the curtains of the Throne of the Lord of Might, which surround His Throne. They are the veil of creation, from the light of the veils and the light of the Throne. Were it not so, the light of the Throne and the light of the veils would burn whatever is beneath the Throne of God's creation. What you have not seen is greater and more marvelous." I said: "Glory be to God, how many are the wonders of His creation!"

I said: "O Jibril, who are the angels you saw in those seas, rows after rows, as if they were a solid structure (Qur'an 61:4)?"

He said: "O Messenger of God, they are the spiritual beings (al-Ruhaniyyun) of whom God says: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾ (Qur'an 78:38), and among them is the Greatest Spirit." Then after that I said: "O Jibril, who are the single row that is in the highest sea, above all the rows, who have surrounded the Throne?" He said: "They are the Karubiyyun (the cherubim), the nobles and greatest of the angels, and none of the angels dares to look at one of the Karubiyyun. Their station is greater than I can describe to you, and what you have seen of them suffices."

Then Jibril took me around Paradise by God's permission. Wherever I descended, I saw it, and he informed me about it. I saw palaces of pearls, rubies, brocade and chrysolite, and I saw trees of red gold, whose branches were pearls and whose roots were silver, firmly set in musk. I know every palace, house, chamber, tent, river and fruit in Paradise better than I know this mosque of mine.

He said: "I saw a river issuing from its source, its water whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, over pebbles of pearl, ruby and pungent musk." Jibril said: "This is al-Kawthar which God, Mighty and Majestic, has given you, and it is al-Tasnim. It flows from their mansions, palaces, houses and chambers, and they mix their drinks with it, of milk, honey and wine. This is His saying: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (Qur'an 83:27–28), and so on."

Then he took me around Paradise until we came to a tree the like of which I had never seen. When I stood beneath it I raised my head, and I could see nothing of my Lord's creation except it, because of its greatness and the spreading of its branches. I found in it a pleasant fragrance, and I had never smelled anything more fragrant in Paradise. I turned my gaze over it, and its leaves were rare garments of the garments of Paradise, of white, red and green. Its fruits were like great jars, of every fruit God created in the heavens and the earths, of many colours, many tastes and many scents. I marvelled at that tree and at its beauty. I said: "O Jibril, what is this tree?" He said: "This is the one God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿Blessed is their lot, and a good place of return﴾ (Qur'an 13:29). Many of your community and your kin will be in its shade, a good resting place and lasting bliss. In Paradise I saw what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. All of that is kept ready and awaits its owner, from among God's friends, Mighty and Majestic." What I saw did not grieve me. I said: ﴿For the likes of this let the workers work﴾ (Qur'an 37:61).

Then the Fire was displayed to me until I looked at its shackles, chains, serpents, scorpions, ghassaq and yahmum. I looked, and there were people with lips like the lips of camels, and someone had been appointed to take hold of their lips, and then they would place in their mouths a stone of fire which came out of their lower parts. I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "These are the ones who consume the property of orphans unjustly."

Then I went on and saw people with bellies like houses, and they were on the road of the people of Pharaoh. When the people of Pharaoh passed by them, they rose up, and one of them would be thrown down by his belly, and the people of Pharaoh would trample them with their feet, while they were exposed to the Fire morning and evening. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the consumers of usury, and their likeness is that of one whom Satan has driven mad by his touch (Qur'an 2:275)."

Then I went on and saw women hanging by their breasts with their feet upturned. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the women who committed adultery and killed their children."

Then he brought me out of Paradise, and we passed through the heavens, descending from one heaven to another, until I came to Musa. He said: "What did God enjoin on you and your community?" I said: "Fifty prayers." Musa said: "I know people better than you do. I [governed] the children of Israel and dealt with them with the utmost difficulty, and your community is the weakest of nations. Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the burden for your community, for your community will not be able to bear it." He said: "So I returned to my Lord."

In some reports: "I returned and came to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and I fell prostrate. I said: 'O Lord, You have enjoined on me and my community fifty prayers, and neither I nor my community will be able to perform them, so lighten ten for me.' I returned to Musa, and he asked me, and I said: 'He lightened ten for me.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it, for your community is the weakest of nations, and I have indeed suffered severe hardship from the children of Israel.' So I returned, and He reduced it to thirty. I kept going between my Lord and Musa (peace be upon him) until He made it five prayers. Then I came to Musa (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it.' I said: 'I have already returned to my Lord until I am ashamed, and I will not go back to Him.'" He said:

"I was called: 'I, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, enjoined on you and your community fifty prayers, and the Word is not changed before Me. So five for fifty. Perform them, you and your community. I have confirmed My obligation and lightened it for My servants, and I reward a good deed tenfold, so each prayer is ten prayers.'" He said: "Muhammad ﷺ was entirely content, and Musa (peace be upon him) was among the most insistent on it when he passed by him, and the most considerate toward them when he returned to him."

Then I departed with my companion and brother Jibril, neither he leaving me nor I leaving him, until he brought me back to my resting place. All of that took place in a single night from your nights here. I am the master of the children of Adam, and without boasting; in my hand is the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and without boasting; and to me are the keys of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and without boasting. I am soon to be taken, after what I have seen. I have seen some of the greatest signs of my Lord that I have seen, and I have longed to meet my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and to meet those of my brothers whom I have seen, and what I have seen of God's reward for His friends. ﴿What is with God is better and more lasting﴾ (Qur'an 28:60).

He said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ returned on the night of his Night Journey, and he was at Dhu Tuwa, he said: "O Jibril, my people will not believe me."

He said: "Abu Bakr will believe you, and he is al-Siddiq (the Truthful) (may God be pleased with him)."

Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha (may God be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the night of my Night Journey came and I awoke in Makkah, I was disheartened about my affair, and I knew that the people would call me a liar."

He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sat apart, grieving, and Abu Jahl, the enemy of God, passed by him, came to him and sat down with him, and said, mocking: "Have you gained anything?" He said: "Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey tonight." He said: "Where to?" He said: "To Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "Then you woke up among us?" He said: "Yes." Abu Jahl denied it, fearing that he would be disbelieved... the hadith. He said: "Will you tell your people what you have told me?"

He said: "Yes." Abu Jahl said: "O assembly of the Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, come here!"

He said: So the gatherings broke up and they came and sat down with the two of them. He said: "Tell your people what you told me." He said:

"Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey tonight." They said: "Where to?" He said: "To Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "Then you woke up among us?" He said: "Yes." He said: Some clapped their hands, and some put their hands on their heads, astonished at the lie. Some of those who had believed in him and affirmed him apostatised, and some men of the polytheists went to Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) and said: "Do you want to hear about your companion who claims that he was taken on a Night Journey tonight to Bayt al-Maqdis?"

He said: "Has he said that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth." They said: "Do you affirm that he went to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night and came back before morning?" He said: "Yes, I affirm him even in what is more remote than that: I affirm him in the news of heaven, in its morning and evening." Therefore Abu Bakr was named al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him).

He said: Among the people were some who had travelled there and some who had visited the mosque, and they said: "Can you describe the mosque to us?" He said: "Yes."

He said: So I began describing and describing, and I kept describing until it became confused for me.

He said: Then the mosque was brought, and I was looking at it, until it was placed before the house of 'Aqil or 'Aqal. So I described the mosque while I was looking at it. The people said: "As for the description, by God he has hit it right."

Then they said: "O Muhammad, tell us about our caravan. It is more important to us than your words. Did you encounter anything in it?" He said: "Yes, I passed by the caravan of the Banu so-and-so, and it was at al-Rawha, and they had lost a camel of theirs, and they were searching for it, and in their saddlebags was a bowl of water. I was thirsty, so I took it and drank, then I put it back as it was. Ask them whether they found the water in the bowl when they returned to it."

They said: "This is one sign." He said: "And I passed by the caravan of so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so, riding camels, and their camels were kneeling with them at Banu Murrah, and their camel bolted from me, so I knocked down so-and-so, and his hand was broken. Ask them about that."

They said: "This is another sign."

They said: "Tell us about our caravan." He said: "I passed by it at al-Ni'aym." They said: "What is its number, its loads, and its flocks?" He said: "I was occupied with something of that, then it was shown to me as if it were the camel with its litter, and I described its number, its loads, its appearance, and who was in it." He said: "Yes, its appearance was such and such, and in it were so-and-so and so-and-so, and in front of it was a grey camel with two patched sacks, and it will come upon you at sunrise."

They said: "This is a sign." Then they went out running towards [the three] saying: "By God, Muhammad has related something and made it clear," until they reached Kada and sat down on it, looking to see when the sun would rise, to disprove him. Then one of them said: "The sun has risen!" Another said: "And these camels have arrived, led by a grey camel, and in it are so-and-so and so-and-so, just as he told them." Yet they did not believe, and they did not prosper, and they said: ﴿We never heard of this in former times; this is nothing but manifest magic﴾ (Qur'an 28:36).

End of the Mi'raj, and to God belongs praise and grace.

If it is said: God only said ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque﴾ (Qur'an 17:1), so why did he say that he was taken up to heaven?

The answer: He said, "He took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque," meaning that the beginning of the matter of the Mi'raj was the Isra' (the Night Journey), and the 'uruj (the ascent) was after the Isra'. The Messenger ﷺ informed them, and he is the truthful and the believed. The wisdom in it, and God knows best, is that had he first informed them of his ascent to heaven, their denial would have been severe and the matter would have been too great in their hearts, and they would not have believed him. So he told them about Bayt al-Maqdis first. When that settled in their hearts and his truthfulness became clear to them, and the proof was established against them, he informed them of his ascent to the highest heaven and the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and in corroboration of ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was two bow-lengths away or nearer﴾ (Qur'an 53:8–9), and ﴿We gave Musa the Book﴾ (Qur'an 17:2) as We took Muhammad ﷺ by night, and ﴿We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾ (Qur'an 17:2), the verse meaning ﴿that you should not take besides Me a guardian﴾ (Qur'an 17:2), that is, a lord, a partner, or a trustee.

The common readers recite it as "yattakhidu" with the ya', meaning: We told them, "Let them not take."

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Abu 'Amr read it with the ya', and Abu 'Ubayd preferred it, saying: "Because it is a report about them: ﴿O offspring of those whom We carried with Nuh; he was indeed a grateful servant﴾ (Qur'an 17:3), whom We saved from the Flood."

The exegetes said: When Nuh (peace be upon him) put on a garment, ate food or drank a drink, he would say: "Praise be to God," and so he was named ﴿a grateful servant﴾.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related from 'Imran ibn Sulaym, who said: Nuh (peace be upon him) was named ﴿a grateful servant﴾ only because when he ate food he said: "Praise be to God who fed me, and if He had willed He would have made me hungry." When he drank he said: "Praise be to God who gave me to drink, and if He had willed He would have made me thirsty." When he was clothed he said: "Praise be to God who clothed me, and if He had willed He would have left me naked." When he was guided he said: "Praise be to God who guided me, and if He had willed He would not have guided me." When he relieved himself he said: "Praise be to God who expelled the filth from me in well-being, and if He had willed He would have kept it in."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 3):

Makkan. It has six thousand, four hundred and sixty letters, one thousand, five hundred and thirty-three words, and one hundred and eleven verses.

Zayd ibn Aslam related from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat Bani Isra'il, his heart will be softened at the mention of the two parents, and he will be given in Paradise two qintars of reward. A qintar is one thousand and two hundred ounces, and one ounce of it is better than the world and whatever is in it." [15] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 6/213.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾.

It was related from Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the meaning of "Subhan Allah." He said: "The declaration of Allah's transcendence above every evil."

"Subhan" may also be used to express wonder. Al-A'sha said:

"I say, when there came to me a boast: 'Glory be to him, from 'Alqamah the boaster!'"

In some hadith, the meaning of "Subhan Allah" is given as: the clearing of Allah from evil. [[In the margin of the manuscript: "Subhan" is a proper name for glorification, like "Uthman" for a man. Its position is that of a verb suppressed and omitted from mention, its estimated form being: "Sabbih Allah" (glorify Allah), "Subhan" then mentioned in the position of the verb, thus indicating the transcendence of Allah above all the ugly acts which His enemies commit.]]

Thus the verse includes both meanings together.

﴿From the Sacred Mosque﴾. Scholars differ regarding this. Some said: The night journey of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was from the Mosque of Makkah.

What supports this is that Qatadah related from Anas, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "While I was in the Sacred Mosque, in the Hijr beside the House, between sleep and wakefulness, Jibril came to me with al-Buraq..." and he mentioned the hadith of the Ascension. [16] [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/157, and Tarikh Baghdad: 11/257.]]

Others said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended from the house of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, sister of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and her husband Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi.

They said: The meaning of His words "from the Sacred Mosque" is "from the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram)," because the whole Haram is a mosque.

What supports this is that al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Badhan, from Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, that she used to say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not make the night journey except while he was sleeping in my house that night. He prayed the late night prayer (al-'isha') in my house, and I prayed with him. Then I got up and slept, leaving him at his prayer place, and I did not wake until he woke me for the dawn prayer. He said:

'Get up, O Umm Hani, I will tell you a wonder.'

I said: 'Every one of your accounts is a wonder, may my father and mother be your ransom!' He stood and prayed the dawn prayer, and I prayed with him. When he finished he said: 'O Umm Hani, I prayed with you the late night prayer as you saw, then after your sleep Jibril came to me while I was in this prayer place and said: O Muhammad, go out. I went out to the door and there was a angel riding an animal, and he said to me:

Mount! I mounted, and it carried me to Bayt al-Maqdis. When I came to a valley, the animal's forelegs stretched and its hind legs shortened; when I came to a height, its hind legs stretched and its forelegs shortened, until I reached Bayt al-Maqdis, and I prayed there. Then I prayed the dawn prayer with you now, as you see me.'" [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/77, and al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 4/165.]]

Muqatil said: The night of the Isra' was a year before the Hijrah.

﴿To the Farthest Mosque﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis. It was called "farthest" because it is the most distant of the mosques that are visited. ﴿The one whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ with water, rivers, trees and fruits.

Mujahid said: It was named blessed because it is the abode of the prophets, the place of descent of the angels and of revelation, it contains the Rock, and from it people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That We might show him some of Our signs﴾, that is, the wonders of Our command. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾

As for the hadith of the Night Journey, I have confined myself to the transmitted and well-known reports, leaving aside the rejected reports and the narrations of weak chains, and I have arranged them in a single concise sequence, so that they may be more pleasing to hear and more beneficial. It is what:

Al-Zuhri related from Ibn Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said.

Al-Suddi related from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, from Badhan, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with some of their words entering into others, they said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the night I was taken by night came, while I was in Makkah between sleep and wakefulness, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, arise.' I got up, and there was Jibril and with him Mika'il. Jibril said to Mika'il: 'Bring me a basin of Zamzam water, so that he may be purified (wa-'attara qalbahu)' [[So it is in the original.]] 'and I may open his breast for him.' He said: So he split open my belly, washed it three times, and Mika'il brought him three basins of Zamzam water. He opened my breast, removed what was in it of rancor, filled it with forbearance, knowledge and faith, and sealed between my shoulders with the seal of prophethood. Then Jibril took my hand until he brought me to the watering place of Zamzam, and he said to an angel: 'Bring me light from Zamzam water and from the water of al-Kawthar.' He said: [The angel said]: 'Perform ablution.' I performed ablution, then he said to me: 'Set out, O Muhammad.' I said: 'To where?' He said: 'To your Lord and the Lord of everything.' He took my hand and brought me out of the mosque, and there I was with al-Buraq, an animal above a donkey and below a mule, its cheek like a human's cheek, its tail like a camel's tail, its mane like a horse's mane, its legs like the legs of camels, its hooves like the hooves of cattle, its chest like a red ruby, its back like a white pearl, on it a saddle of the saddles of Paradise, and it had two wings on its thighs; it moves like lightning, each step as far as the eye can reach. He said to me: 'Mount.' It was the animal of Ibrahim with which he used to visit the Sacred House.

He said: When I placed my hands upon it, it shied (shammasa) [[Shammasat al-dabbah: it fled and bolted and turned its back.]] and resisted me. Jibril said: 'Calm down, O Buraq.' Al-Buraq said: 'O Jibril, [did anyone touch my back?]' [[So it is in the original.]] Jibril said: 'Have you touched [its back]?' [[So it is in the original.]] He said: 'No, by Allah, except that I once passed by a [group of camels] and I wiped my hand over their heads and said:

"Indeed, a people who worship you besides Allah are in error."' Jibril said: 'O Buraq, are you not ashamed? By Allah, no one has ever mounted you, since there was a prophet, who is more honored by Allah than Muhammad (ﷺ).' He said: So al-Buraq trembled and broke into sweat out of shame before me, then lowered itself to me until it touched the ground. I mounted it and sat upright on it. Jibril set out with me toward the Farthest Mosque, with the strides of al-Buraq covering as far as the eye can see. It kept pace beside me, not outrunning me, nor did I outrun it. While I was on my journey, a voice called to me from my right, saying: 'O Muhammad, wait a moment, let me ask you something.' He called three times, but I did not slow down for him, and I passed on until I had gone beyond him. Then I saw an old woman who had been adorned with every kind of finery and splendor, and she said: 'O Muhammad, come to me!' I did not turn to her, and I said: 'O Jibril, who is this who called me from my right?' He said: 'The summoner of the Jews. If you had answered him, your community would have become Jewish after you. And the one who called you from your left is the summoner of the Christians; if you had answered him, your community would have become Christian after you. As for the one who displayed her splendor and adornment to you, she is the world. If you had turned to her, your community would have chosen the world over the Hereafter.'

Then two vessels were brought to me, one containing milk and the other wine. It was said to me: 'Drink whichever you wish.' I took the milk and drank it. Jibril said to me: 'You have chosen the natural disposition (al-fitrah), you and your community. As for you, had you taken the wine, your community would have become intoxicated after you.'

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proceeded, and Jibril proceeded with him. He passed by a people who were sowing and reaping on the same day; whenever they reaped, it grew back as it was. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Who are these?' He said: 'They are the emigrants in the way of Allah; their good deed is multiplied seven hundred times, and whatever they spend, He replaces it, and He is the best of providers.' [Cf. Qur'an 34:39]

He said: Then he passed by a people whose heads were being crushed with stones; whenever they were crushed, they returned as they were, and nothing of this was relaxed for them. He said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'They are the ones whose heads are heavy against the obligatory prayer.'

Then he passed by a people, in front of them were rags and behind them were rags, and they grazed as cattle graze on the thorny plant (al-dari') and the zaqqum tree, which covers the outside of Hell and its stones. He said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'They are those who do not pay the charity of their wealth. [Allah did not wrong them] ... ﴿and your Lord is not unjust to the servants﴾. [[Surah Fussilat: 46.]]'

Then he passed by a people, before them was meat in a pot, cooked and good, and other meat, foul. They began to eat the foul and leave the cooked good. He said: 'Who are these?' He said: 'This is the man who has a wife who is lawful and good, yet he goes to a foul woman and spends the night with her until morning; and the woman rises from her husband, who is lawful and good, and goes to the foul man and spends the night with him until morning.'

Then he passed by [a woman] on the road, and no garment passed by her without being torn, and nothing else without being shredded. He said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is the likeness of your community who sit on the road and cut off people by the like of ﴿and do not sit on every path threatening﴾ [[Surah al-A'raf: 56.]] and so on.'

Then he passed by a man who had gathered a great bundle he could not carry, yet he kept adding to it. He said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is a man of your community upon whom are the trusts of people; he cannot discharge them, yet he keeps adding to them.'

Then he passed by a people whose tongues and lips were being cut with scissors of iron; whenever they were cut, they returned as they were. He said: 'Who are these?' He said: 'These are the preachers of sedition.'

Then he passed by a small stone from which a great bull came out. The bull wanted to return to where it came from, but could not.

He said: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is a man of your community who speaks a grave word and then regrets it, and cannot take it back.'

He said: Then he came to a valley and found a pleasant, cool scent and a sound. He said: 'What is this pleasant scent and this sound?' He said: 'This is the sound of Paradise.' He said: 'My Lord, show me what You have promised me, for my mansions, my silk, my brocade, my fine silk, my lush cloth, my pearls, my corals, my silver, my gold, my cups, my platters, my jugs, my fruits, my honey, my milk, my wine and my water have multiplied; so bring me what You have promised me.' It was said to him: 'For you is every believing man and woman who believed in Me and My messengers, did righteous deeds, did not associate anything with Me, and did not take rivals besides Me. Whoever fears Me is safe; whoever asks Me, I give him; whoever lends to Me, I repay him; whoever relies upon Me, I suffice him. Indeed, I am Allah; there is no god but I; I do not break My promise. ﴿The believers have succeeded.﴾ ﴿Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾' He said: 'I am content.'

He said: Then he came to a valley and heard a terrible sound and found a foul smell. He said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is the sound of Hell, saying: [O Lord, bring me] [[From the tafsir of al-Tabari: 15/12.]] what You have promised me, for my chains, my shackles, my blaze, my boiling water, my thorny plant, my pus and my torment have multiplied, my depth has grown distant and my heat has intensified; so bring me what You have promised me.' He said: 'For you is every polytheist, male and female, every disbelieving man and woman, every wicked man and woman, and every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.'

She said: 'I am content, O Lord.' Then he proceeded, and Jibril with him. Jibril said to him: 'Descend and pray.' He said: So I descended and prayed. He said: 'Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Taybah, and to it is the emigration to Allah.' Then he said: 'Descend and pray.' So I descended and prayed. He said: 'Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Mount Sinai, where Allah spoke to Musa.' Then he said: 'Descend and pray.' So I descended and prayed. He said: 'Do you know where you prayed? You prayed at Bethlehem, where Isa (peace be upon him) was born.'

He said: Then we proceeded until we reached Bayt al-Maqdis. When I arrived there, I found angels who had descended from the heavens, meeting me with good news and honor from the Lord of Might, saying: 'Peace be upon you, O first, O last, O gatherer.' He said: I said: 'O Jibril, what is their greeting to me?' He said: 'You are the first whom the earth will be split open for, and your community; you are the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted; you are the last of the prophets, and the gathering is for you and your community,' meaning the gathering of the Day of Resurrection."

He (ﷺ) said: "Then we passed them until we reached the door of the mosque. Jibril brought me down and tied al-Buraq to the ring to which the prophets used to tie their mounts, with a rope of Paradise's silk. When I entered the door, there I found the prophets and messengers."[18] [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/10–16.]]

In the hadith of Abu al-'Aliyah: "The spirits of the prophets and messengers whom Allah sent before me, from Idris and Nuh to Isa, had been gathered by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They greeted me and welcomed me with a greeting like the greeting of the angels. I said: 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'Your brothers the prophets. Quraysh claimed that Allah has a partner, and the Jews and Christians claimed that Allah has a son. Ask these messengers: Is there a partner of Allah?' This is His saying, ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Gracious?﴾ [[Surah al-Zukhruf: 45.]] So they acknowledged the lordship of Allah, the Exalted. Then He gathered them and the angels in rows, and He put me forward and commanded me to lead them in prayer, and I led them in two rak'ahs.

Then the prophets praised their Lord. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has taken me as a friend, given me a great kingdom, made me a devout community to be followed, rescued me from the Fire, and made it cool and safe for me.﴾ Then Musa (peace be upon him) praised his Lord and said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, who spoke to me directly, made the destruction of Pharaoh and the deliverance of the Children of Israel through my hands, and made from my community a people who guide by the truth and act justly by it. Then Dawud (peace be upon him) praised his Lord and said: 'All praise is for Allah, who has given me a great kingdom, taught me the Psalms, made iron soft for me, subjected the mountains to glorify with me, and the birds, and given me ﴿wisdom and decisive speech﴾.' Then Sulayman (peace be upon him) praised his Lord and said: 'All praise is for Allah, who subjected the winds to me, subjected to me the jinn who work for me as I wish, ﴿such as sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs, and fixed cooking pots﴾, taught me the speech of birds, gave me abundance of everything, and gave me a great kingdom ﴿such as none shall have after me﴾, and made my kingdom a good kingdom with no reckoning upon me.'

Then Isa (peace be upon him) praised his Lord and said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, who made me a word from Him, made me create from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah, made me heal the blind and the leper and give life to the dead by the permission of Allah, raised me up, purified me, protected me and my mother from the accursed Satan, so Satan had no authority over us.'

Then Muhammad (ﷺ) said: 'All of you have praised your Lord, and I too praise my Lord.' He said: 'All praise is for Allah, who sent me as ﴿a mercy to the worlds﴾ and ﴿to all mankind as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾, sent down the Qur'an to me (in it is the explanation of everything), made my community ﴿the best community brought forth for mankind﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 143.]] and made my community ﴿a middle nation﴾ [[Surah Al 'Imran: 110.]], made my community the first and the last, opened my breast, removed from me my burden, raised my remembrance, and made me the opener and the seal.'

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'With this, Muhammad is the best of you.' Then three vessels with covered mouths were brought: one contained water, and it was said to him: 'Drink,' and he drank a little from it. Then another vessel containing milk was handed to him, and it was said to him: 'Drink,' and he drank from it until he was satisfied. Then another vessel containing wine was handed to him, and it was said to him: 'Drink,' but he said: 'I do not want it; I am satisfied.' Jibril said to him: 'You are right. As for it, it will be forbidden to your community; had you drunk from it, only a few of your community would have followed you; and had you been satisfied with the water, you and your community would have drowned.'

Then Jibril (peace be upon him) took my hand and went with me to the Rock, and he ascended with me onto it, and there was a ladder to the heaven, the like of which I had never seen in beauty and loveliness; the onlookers had never looked upon anything more beautiful than it. It is the ladder ﴿by which the angels ascend﴾; its base is on the Rock of Bayt al-Maqdis and its top is joined to the heaven. One of its sides is a red ruby and the other a green emerald; a step of silver, a step of gold and a step of emerald, adorned with pearls and rubies. It is the ladder from which the Angel of Death goes forth to take the souls [...] [[So it is in the original.]] knowledge departs from him when he sees it, because of its beauty. Then Jibril lifted me and placed me on his wing, then he rose with me from that ladder to the lowest heaven. He knocked at the door, and it was said: 'Who is it?' He said: 'I am Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.'

He said: "Has Muhammad indeed been sent?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Welcome to him. May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came." He opened the door and we entered.

He said: "While I was traveling through the lowest heaven, I saw a rooster with green down and a white head, its feathers as white as the most intense white I had ever seen, and beneath its feathers green down as intensely green as I had ever seen. And there was a man at the bottom of the seventh lowest earth, whose head was at the Throne, his neck bent beneath the Throne. He had two wings from his shoulders, and when he spread them he would extend beyond the East and the West. When he was in some [mile] he spread his wings, beat them, and cried out in glorification of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'Glory be to the King, the Holy, the Great, the Exalted. There is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting.' When he did this, all the roosters of the earth glorified Him, beat their wings, and began to crow. When that rooster in the heavens fell silent, all the roosters of the earth fell silent. Then, when he stirred again in the heavens in the manner they had done, the roosters of the earth crowed in response, glorifying Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with words like his."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ever since I saw that rooster, I have longed to see it again."

He said: "Then I passed by an angel, half of whose body, on the side of his head, was fire, and the other half was ice, with a barrier between them. Neither does the fire melt the ice, nor does the ice extinguish the fire. He was standing and calling out with a beautiful, lofty voice: 'O Allah, who joins the ice and the fire, join the hearts of Your believing servants.'"

I said: "O Jibril, who is this?" He said: "An angel called Habib, whom Allah has appointed over the regions of the heavens and the edges of the earths. How sincerely he advises the people of the earth; he has said this since Allah, Exalted is He, created him."

He said: "Then I passed by another angel sitting on a chair, with the world gathered between his knees. In his hands was a tablet of light, which he gazed at, not turning right or left, gazing at it like one in grief. I said: 'Who is this, O Jibril? I have not passed by any angle I feared more than him; is there anything like this?' He said: 'What prevents you? We are all in your position. This is the Angel of Death, constantly engaged in seizing souls, and he is the most diligent of the angels in his work.' I said: 'O Jibril, does everyone who dies look upon this?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Death is enough of a calamity.' He said: 'O Muhammad, what comes after death is even greater and more terrible.' I said: 'O Jibril, bring me near the Angel of Death so I may greet him and ask him.' He brought me near him, and I greeted him. He gestured to me, and Jibril said to him: 'This is Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy and the Messenger of the Arabs.' He welcomed me, greeted me, and gave me the glad tidings and honor. He said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, for I see all good in your community.' I said: 'Praise be to Allah, the Bestower of blessings. What is this tablet before you?' He said: 'It contains the appointed terms of all creatures.'

I said: 'Then where are the names of those whose souls you seized in the bygone ages?' He said: 'They are in another tablet, whose creation I know. That is why I act upon every living being: when its soul is seized, I have finished with it.' I said: 'O Angel of Death, glory be to Allah! How can you seize the souls of all the people of the earth while you remain in this place without moving?' He said: 'Do you not see that the whole world is between my knees, and all creatures are before my eyes, and my hands reach the East and the West and what they contain? When the term of any servant of Allah runs out, I look at him and at my helpers. When my helpers among the angels look at me, and I look at him, they know he is to be seized. They then go to him to extract his soul. When the soul reaches the throat, I know it, and nothing of my affairs is hidden from me. I extend my hand to him and seize him; none but I may seize him. That is my task and the task of the living beings among the servants of Allah.'"

He said: "It was only his words that made me weep, while I was with him. Then we passed on and came to another angel. I had never seen any angel like him: his face was sullen, his appearance hideous, his strength fierce, and his anger evident. When he looked at me, I was startled and feared him greatly. I asked: 'O Jibril, who is this?' He said: 'Do not be surprised that you are frightened of him; we are all in your position of fear of him. This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. He has never smiled, and since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appointed him over Hell, he has grown angrier and more furious every day against the enemies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the people of disobedience to Him, so that he may take vengeance upon them.'

I said: 'Bring me close to him.' He brought me close to him, and Jibril greeted him, but he did not raise his head. Jibril said: 'O Malik, this is Muhammad, the Messenger of the Arabs.' He looked at me, greeted me, and gave me good tidings. I said: 'How long have you been standing over Hell?' He said: 'Since I was created until now, and so it will be until the Hour arrives.' I said: 'O Jibril, I wish to see a glimpse of the Fire.' He ordered it, and it did so. A blazing, black flame came forth, with murky, dark smoke, which filled the horizons. I saw a great terror and a dreadful matter, which I am unable to describe to you. I fainted and nearly lost my life. Jibril embraced me and commanded that the Fire be returned, and it was returned."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We passed on and came to many angels whose number none can count except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Some of them had faces between their shoulders and faces on their chests, and every face had mouths and tongues. They praised Allah and glorified Him with those tongues. I saw among their bodies, their forms and their worship, a tremendous wonder. We then passed on, and there was a man of perfect creation, lacking nothing of the creation of human beings. On his right was a door from which a good fragrance came forth, and on his left was a door from which a foul odor came forth. When he looked at the door on his right, he laughed; when he looked at the door on his left, he wept in sorrow. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this, and what are these two doors?' He said: 'This is your father Adam (peace be upon him). The door on his right is the gate of Paradise. When he looks at those of his descendants who enter Paradise, he laughs and rejoices. The door on his left is the gate of Hell. When he looks at those of his descendants who enter Hell, he weeps and grieves.'

Then we ascended to the second heaven, and Jibril (peace be upon him) asked for entry. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming.' We entered and saw two youths. I said: 'O Jibril, who are these two youths?' He said: 'These are Isa and Yahya, cousins on the mother's side.'

Then I ascended to the third heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' We entered and saw a man who was endowed above people with beauty, like the finest moon on the night of the full moon above the other stars. I said: 'Who is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is your brother Yusuf (peace be upon him).'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then I was taken up to the fourth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' We entered and saw a man in a [kadha] state. I said: 'Who is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is Idris, whom Allah raised to a lofty place,' and he was leaning his back against the registers of the creatures, in which their affairs are recorded.

Then I was taken up to the fifth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.'

Then we entered and saw a man sitting, around whom were people he was recounting to. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this, and who are those around him?' He said: 'This is Harun, the beloved [al-Muhabbab], and those around him are the Children of Israel.'"

"Then we ascended to the sixth heaven, and he asked for entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' Then we entered and saw a man sitting. We passed by him, and the man wept. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this?' He said: 'This is Musa.' I said: 'Why is he weeping?' He said: 'The Children of Israel claim that I am the most honored of the children of Adam before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This man is a man of the children of Adam, and he has been left behind by me in his worldly life, while I am in my afterlife. If it were only himself, I would not mind, but with every prophet there is his community.'"

He said: "Then I was taken up to the seventh heaven, and he asked for entry. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Has Muhammad been sent?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'May God greet him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother, how excellent a successor, and how excellent his coming, he came.' Then we entered and saw a man [grey-haired] sitting on a chair at the gate of Paradise. Around him were people sitting with [white] faces like sheets of paper, and other people in whose complexions there was something [...] [[A blank in the manuscript. In Tafsir al-Tabari (15/15) the speech is continuous, and in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/71) there is an addition: 'Isa, i.e. Abu Ja'far al-Razi, said: I heard him say once: black faces.']]

Those in whose complexions there was something stood up, entered a river, bathed in it, and came out, and some of the something had left their complexions. Then they entered another river, bathed in it, and came out, and it had completely left their complexions, which became like the complexions of their companions. They came and sat beside their companions. I said: 'O Jibril, who is this grey-haired man, who are these people, and what are these rivers?' He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the first to turn grey upon the earth. As for these white-faced people, they are a people who have not mixed their faith with wrongdoing. As for those who had something in their complexions, they are a people who mixed righteous deeds with others that were evil, then repented, and Allah accepted their repentance. As for the three rivers: the first is the mercy of Allah, the second is the blessing of Allah, and the third is "their Lord gave them a pure drink." He said: Then I found Ibrahim leaning against a house, and I asked Jibril. He said: This is the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur), which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and when they leave it they never return to it again.'

He said: 'Then Jibril brought me until we reached the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). There I saw a tree whose single leaf covered the world with what it contains, and its fruit was like the jars of Hajar. Four rivers emerged from its root: two apparent and two hidden. I asked Jibril about them. He said: "As for the two hidden ones, they are in Paradise. As for the two apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates." Also from its root come "rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste does not alter, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey." It lies at the edge of the seventh heaven; Paradise, its roots and its branches are beneath the Throne.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reached the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I knew that it was the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I knew its leaves and its fruit. There covered it of the light of Allah what covered it, and the angels covered it like locusts of gold out of fear of Allah, Exalted is He. When what covered it covered it, it transformed until no one could prevent it. He said: There are angels in it whose number none knows except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the station of Jibril is in its midst. When I reached it, Jibril said to me: 'Go forward!' I said: 'Forward of whom? You go forward, O Muhammad, for you are more honored by Allah than I am.' I went forward, with Jibril following my steps, until he brought me to a veil of gold brocade, and he shook the veil. It said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'I am Jibril, and with me is Muhammad.' The angel said: 'Allah is greater.' He extended his hand from beneath the veil, lifted me up, and left Jibril behind. I said to him: 'Where are you taking me?' He said: 'O Muhammad, "There is none of us but has a known station." This is the limit of the creatures. I was only permitted to approach the veil out of respect for you and because of your majesty.'"

He said: "Then the angel carried me, faster than the blink of an eye, to a veil of pearls, and he shook the veil. The angel said from behind the veil: 'Who is this?' He said: 'I am the keeper of the gold brocade, and with me is Muhammad, the Messenger of the Arabs.' The angel said: 'Allah is greater,' and extended his hand from beneath the veil, lifted me up, and placed me before Him. I continued thus from veil to veil until they had brought me past seventy veils. The thickness of each veil was a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between one veil and the next was a five-hundred-year journey. Then a green canopy was lowered for me, whose light overcame the light of the sun, and my sight was dazzled. I was placed upon that canopy, and it carried me until it brought me to the Throne. When I saw the Throne, everything near the Throne became clear. Allah brought me close to the support of the Throne, and a drop from the Throne descended and settled upon my tongue. No one who has tasted anything has ever tasted anything sweeter than it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed me by it of the news of the first and the last. Allah loosed my tongue, which had been stilled by awe of the Most Merciful. I said: 'All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah.' Allah, Exalted is He, said: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' I said: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.' He said: 'O Muhammad, do you know about what the Exalted Assembly disputed?' I said: 'You, O Lord, know best about that and about everything, and You are the Knower of the unseen.' He said: 'They disputed about the ranks and the good deeds. Do you know, O Muhammad, what the ranks and the good deeds are?' I said: 'You know best, O Lord.' He said: 'The ranks are completing the ablution in difficult conditions, walking on foot to congregations, and waiting for prayers after prayers. The good deeds are spreading peace, feeding food, and performing the night prayer while people sleep.' Then He said: 'O Muhammad, "The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord"?' I said: 'Yes, O Lord.' He said: 'And the believers?' I said: '"Each believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers; we make no distinction between any of His messengers," as the Jews and Christians made distinctions.' He said: 'What did they say?' I said: '"We hear and we obey." ' He said: 'You have spoken truly; ask and you will be given.' I said: '"Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return."' He said: 'I have forgiven you and your community. Ask and you will be given.' I said: '"Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err."' He said: 'I have lifted the error and forgetfulness from you and your community, and what they are compelled to.' I said: '"Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear."' He said: 'I have done that for you and your community.' I said: '"Our Lord, pardon us from being swallowed up by the earth, forgive us from being struck down by a calamity, and have mercy on us from being transformed. You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelieving people."' He said: 'I have done that for you and your community.' Then it was said to me: 'Ask.'

I said: 'O Lord, You took Ibrahim as a friend, You spoke to Musa directly, You raised Idris to a lofty place, You gave Sulayman a great kingdom, and You gave Dawud the Psalms. What then is mine, O Lord?' My Lord said: 'O Muhammad, I have taken you as a friend as I took Ibrahim as a friend, and I have spoken to you as I spoke to Musa directly. I have given you the Opening of the Book and the final verses of al-Baqarah, which were among the treasures of the Throne, and I have not given them to any prophet before you. I have sent you to the people of the earth, all of them, white and black, humankind and jinn, and I did not send any prophet to all of them before you. I have made the entire earth, its land and its sea, pure and a place of prostration for you and your community. I have fed you and your community from the spoils, and I did not feed any community before them. I have aided you with terror against your enemy from a distance of a month's journey. I have sent down to you the chief of all the books and its guardian, "a Qur'an We have divided." I have raised your remembrance, so you are remembered whenever I am remembered in the laws of My religion. I have given you in place of the Torah the oft-repeated (al-mathani), in place of the Gospel the manifest, and in place of the Psalms the Hawamim. I have favored you with the detailed (al-mufassal), I have expanded your breast, I have removed your burden, and I have made your community "the best community brought forth for humankind," and I have made them "a middle nation," and I have made them the first, while they are the last. So take what I have given you, and be among the thankful.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then He entrusted me, after that, with a covenant concerning matters which I was not permitted to tell you. Then fifty prayers were enjoined upon me and my community each day and night. When He had testified to me of His covenant and left me in His presence for as long as He willed, He said to me: 'Return to your people and convey My message to them.' The green canopy on which I had been carried took me, lowering and raising me, until it swept me down to the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary. There I saw Jibril (peace be upon him) behind me with my heart, just as I saw him in front of me with my eyes. Jibril said to me: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, for you are the best of Allah's creation and His chosen one among the prophets. May Allah greet you with what He has not greeted anyone of His creation, neither a near angel nor a sent prophet. He has placed you in a station that none of the people of the heavens and the earth has reached. May Allah congratulate you on His honor and on the preeminent station and the surpassing dignity He has bestowed upon you. So take it and give thanks, for Allah is a Bestower who loves the thankful.'"

I praised God for that. Then Jibril said to me: "Go, O Muhammad, to Paradise, so that I may show you what is prepared for you in it, so that you may grow in asceticism in this world to match your asceticism, and in desire for the Hereafter to match your desire." So we set off, descending swiftly, faster than an arrow and the wind, until by God's permission we reached Paradise. My soul was calmed, and my heart returned to me. I began to ask Jibril about what I had seen in Paradise of seas, fire, light and other things, and he said:

"Glory be to God! Those are the curtains of the Throne of the Lord of Might, which surround His Throne. They are the veil of creation, from the light of the veils and the light of the Throne. Were it not so, the light of the Throne and the light of the veils would burn whatever is beneath the Throne of God's creation. What you have not seen is greater and more marvelous." I said: "Glory be to God, how many are the wonders of His creation!"

I said: "O Jibril, who are the angels you saw in those seas, rows after rows, as if they were a solid structure (Qur'an 61:4)?"

He said: "O Messenger of God, they are the spiritual beings (al-Ruhaniyyun) of whom God says: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾ (Qur'an 78:38), and among them is the Greatest Spirit." Then after that I said: "O Jibril, who are the single row that is in the highest sea, above all the rows, who have surrounded the Throne?" He said: "They are the Karubiyyun (the cherubim), the nobles and greatest of the angels, and none of the angels dares to look at one of the Karubiyyun. Their station is greater than I can describe to you, and what you have seen of them suffices."

Then Jibril took me around Paradise by God's permission. Wherever I descended, I saw it, and he informed me about it. I saw palaces of pearls, rubies, brocade and chrysolite, and I saw trees of red gold, whose branches were pearls and whose roots were silver, firmly set in musk. I know every palace, house, chamber, tent, river and fruit in Paradise better than I know this mosque of mine.

He said: "I saw a river issuing from its source, its water whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, over pebbles of pearl, ruby and pungent musk." Jibril said: "This is al-Kawthar which God, Mighty and Majestic, has given you, and it is al-Tasnim. It flows from their mansions, palaces, houses and chambers, and they mix their drinks with it, of milk, honey and wine. This is His saying: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (Qur'an 83:27–28), and so on."

Then he took me around Paradise until we came to a tree the like of which I had never seen. When I stood beneath it I raised my head, and I could see nothing of my Lord's creation except it, because of its greatness and the spreading of its branches. I found in it a pleasant fragrance, and I had never smelled anything more fragrant in Paradise. I turned my gaze over it, and its leaves were rare garments of the garments of Paradise, of white, red and green. Its fruits were like great jars, of every fruit God created in the heavens and the earths, of many colours, many tastes and many scents. I marvelled at that tree and at its beauty. I said: "O Jibril, what is this tree?" He said: "This is the one God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿Blessed is their lot, and a good place of return﴾ (Qur'an 13:29). Many of your community and your kin will be in its shade, a good resting place and lasting bliss. In Paradise I saw what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. All of that is kept ready and awaits its owner, from among God's friends, Mighty and Majestic." What I saw did not grieve me. I said: ﴿For the likes of this let the workers work﴾ (Qur'an 37:61).

Then the Fire was displayed to me until I looked at its shackles, chains, serpents, scorpions, ghassaq and yahmum. I looked, and there were people with lips like the lips of camels, and someone had been appointed to take hold of their lips, and then they would place in their mouths a stone of fire which came out of their lower parts. I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "These are the ones who consume the property of orphans unjustly."

Then I went on and saw people with bellies like houses, and they were on the road of the people of Pharaoh. When the people of Pharaoh passed by them, they rose up, and one of them would be thrown down by his belly, and the people of Pharaoh would trample them with their feet, while they were exposed to the Fire morning and evening. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the consumers of usury, and their likeness is that of one whom Satan has driven mad by his touch (Qur'an 2:275)."

Then I went on and saw women hanging by their breasts with their feet upturned. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the women who committed adultery and killed their children."

Then he brought me out of Paradise, and we passed through the heavens, descending from one heaven to another, until I came to Musa. He said: "What did God enjoin on you and your community?" I said: "Fifty prayers." Musa said: "I know people better than you do. I [governed] the children of Israel and dealt with them with the utmost difficulty, and your community is the weakest of nations. Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the burden for your community, for your community will not be able to bear it." He said: "So I returned to my Lord."

In some reports: "I returned and came to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and I fell prostrate. I said: 'O Lord, You have enjoined on me and my community fifty prayers, and neither I nor my community will be able to perform them, so lighten ten for me.' I returned to Musa, and he asked me, and I said: 'He lightened ten for me.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it, for your community is the weakest of nations, and I have indeed suffered severe hardship from the children of Israel.' So I returned, and He reduced it to thirty. I kept going between my Lord and Musa (peace be upon him) until He made it five prayers. Then I came to Musa (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it.' I said: 'I have already returned to my Lord until I am ashamed, and I will not go back to Him.'" He said:

"I was called: 'I, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, enjoined on you and your community fifty prayers, and the Word is not changed before Me. So five for fifty. Perform them, you and your community. I have confirmed My obligation and lightened it for My servants, and I reward a good deed tenfold, so each prayer is ten prayers.'" He said: "Muhammad ﷺ was entirely content, and Musa (peace be upon him) was among the most insistent on it when he passed by him, and the most considerate toward them when he returned to him."

Then I departed with my companion and brother Jibril, neither he leaving me nor I leaving him, until he brought me back to my resting place. All of that took place in a single night from your nights here. I am the master of the children of Adam, and without boasting; in my hand is the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and without boasting; and to me are the keys of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and without boasting. I am soon to be taken, after what I have seen. I have seen some of the greatest signs of my Lord that I have seen, and I have longed to meet my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and to meet those of my brothers whom I have seen, and what I have seen of God's reward for His friends. ﴿What is with God is better and more lasting﴾ (Qur'an 28:60).

He said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ returned on the night of his Night Journey, and he was at Dhu Tuwa, he said: "O Jibril, my people will not believe me."

He said: "Abu Bakr will believe you, and he is al-Siddiq (the Truthful) (may God be pleased with him)."

Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha (may God be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the night of my Night Journey came and I awoke in Makkah, I was disheartened about my affair, and I knew that the people would call me a liar."

He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sat apart, grieving, and Abu Jahl, the enemy of God, passed by him, came to him and sat down with him, and said, mocking: "Have you gained anything?" He said: "Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey tonight." He said: "Where to?" He said: "To Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "Then you woke up among us?" He said: "Yes." Abu Jahl denied it, fearing that he would be disbelieved... the hadith. He said: "Will you tell your people what you have told me?"

He said: "Yes." Abu Jahl said: "O assembly of the Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, come here!"

He said: So the gatherings broke up and they came and sat down with the two of them. He said: "Tell your people what you told me." He said:

"Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey tonight." They said: "Where to?" He said: "To Bayt al-Maqdis." He said: "Then you woke up among us?" He said: "Yes." He said: Some clapped their hands, and some put their hands on their heads, astonished at the lie. Some of those who had believed in him and affirmed him apostatised, and some men of the polytheists went to Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) and said: "Do you want to hear about your companion who claims that he was taken on a Night Journey tonight to Bayt al-Maqdis?"

He said: "Has he said that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth." They said: "Do you affirm that he went to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night and came back before morning?" He said: "Yes, I affirm him even in what is more remote than that: I affirm him in the news of heaven, in its morning and evening." Therefore Abu Bakr was named al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him).

He said: Among the people were some who had travelled there and some who had visited the mosque, and they said: "Can you describe the mosque to us?" He said: "Yes."
