We called upon Him like the cooing of doves, and wept like the howling of wolves, yet we are not heard and we are not answered.' God said: 'Ask them what prevents Me from responding to them. Do I not hear the listeners, see the watchers, come nearest to those who answer, and have the most mercy of the merciful? Has My hand now become withered?'

I say: How could it be, when My hands are extended with goodness? I spend as I will, and the keys of the treasuries are with Me; none opens them but Me. Or is it that My mercy has become constricted? How could it be, when My mercy has encompassed everything, and the merciful show mercy only by its bounty? Or is it that [stinginess has overtaken Me]? Or am I not the most generous of the generous and the Opener of good things? I am the most bountiful of givers and the most honorable of those who are asked. If these people had looked at themselves with the wisdom that was illuminated in their hearts, and had not cast it aside and bartered it for this world, they would have seen from where they came, and they would have been certain that their own souls are the greatest of their enemies. So how should I raise their fasting when they clothe it with false speech, and strengthen themselves by it with the sustenance of the unlawful? How should I make their prayer radiant when their hearts incline toward one who wars against Me and violates My sanctities? Or how should their charities be purified with Me, when they give in charity from other people's wealth, and I only reward its rightful owners who were wronged? Or how should I answer their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues, while their deeds are far from it? I answer only the one who calls with gentleness, and I hear the words of the weak and the poor. Indeed, among the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. If they had shown mercy to the poor, drawn near to the weak, given justice to the oppressed, supported the wronged and the defeated, done justice to the absent, and rendered to the orphan, the widow, the needy, and every possessor of a right his right, then, were it fitting for Me to speak to humankind, I would have spoken to them. I would have been the light of their sight, the hearing of their ears, the understanding of their hearts, I would have strengthened their supports, and been the strength of their hands and feet. And their tongues and minds would have been strengthened."

They say, when they heard my words and my messages reached them: "These are fabricated sayings, traditions handed down, and a composition like the composition of sorcerers and soothsayers." They claimed that if they wished, they could bring a discourse like it, and that they could attain knowledge of the unseen. They would be informed by what the devils reveal to them, and they would speak to them, and what is said and kept secret would be hidden. And they would be doing this while I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal. I have decreed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, a decree which I have made binding upon Myself, and I have set beyond it a determined term that will inevitably come to pass. If they truly believe in what they claim of the knowledge of the unseen, then let them inform you when I will execute it, or at what time it will occur. And if they are able to bring about whatever they wish, then let them bring the like of the power by which I have executed it. For I shall make it manifest over all religion, ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verses 4–8 (part 2 of 4):

And if they are able to say whatever they wish, then let them produce the like of the wisdom with which I govern this affair of decree, if you are truthful. For I decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth that I would place prophethood among the lowly, sovereignty in supplication, honor among the abased, strength among the weak, wealth among the poor, abundance among the few, [cities in the wastelands], thickets in the sands, the ... in the pastures, knowledge among the ignorant and judgment among the unlettered. So ask them: when is this, who will uphold it, at whose hand will it be established, and who are the helpers and supporters of this matter, if they know? Indeed, I shall send forth for this a prophet, a non-blind man among the blind and not a misguided one among the misguided. He is neither harsh nor coarse, [nor loud-voiced in the markets], [nor adorned with obscenity], nor one who speaks foul speech. I shall guide him to every good thing. I shall grant him every [noble] character. I shall make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, pardon and kindness his character, justice and kindness his conduct, truth his law, guidance his leader, Islam his creed, and Ahmad his name. Through him I shall guide after misguidance, teach after ignorance, raise up after [abasement], make known after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and bring together hearts that differ, desires that scatter, and nations that are dispersed. I shall make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, out of faith in Me, monotheism for Me, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray to Me standing, sitting, bowing and prostrating. They will fight in My cause in rows and waves, and they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I shall inspire them with glorification, monotheism, praise, commendation and exaltation of Me in their mosques, their gatherings, their beds, their comings and goings, and their dwelling places. They will proclaim My greatness, declare My oneness and sanctify Me in the marketplaces. They will purify for Me their faces and their extremities, and they will tie their garments at the ends. Their offering is their blood, their Gospels are in their chests, they are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I give to whom I will, and Allah is the Owner of great bounty.

When their prophet Sha'ya had finished his address to them, they rushed upon him to kill him, and he fled from them. A tree met him and split open for him, and he entered it. [Satan came upon him in the tree], and he seized the hem of his garment and showed it to them. They placed the saw in its middle and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle. [Allah appointed] over the Children of Israel, after they killed Sha'ya, a man from among them called Nashiyah ibn Amus. And He sent al-Khadir as a prophet to them. The name of al-Khadir is Irmiya ibn Hilqiya, and he was from the tribe of Harun ibn Imran. He was called al-Khadir because he sat upon a white patch of land and it [trembled and became green] when he rose from it. Allah said to Irmiya when He sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel: "O Irmiya, before I created you I chose you, and before I formed you in your mother's womb I sanctified you, and before I brought you out from your mother's womb I purified you." The hadith is mentioned in full, including Irmiya's sermon to his people and the fatwa he issued, and the entry of Bukht Nasr and his armies into Jerusalem, and his trampling of al-Sham, as we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

When Irmiya saw that, he flew away until he mingled with the wild beasts. Bukht Nasr and his armies entered Jerusalem, trampled al-Sham, killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them, and ruined Jerusalem. Then he ordered his soldiers that each man should fill his waterskin with dirt and throw it into Jerusalem, and they threw dirt into it until they filled it. Then he returned to the land of Babylon, taking with him the captives of the Children of Israel. He ordered them to gather everyone who was in Jerusalem, so they gathered before him every young and old person of the Children of Israel, and he chose from them seventy thousand boys.

When the spoils of his army were brought out and he wished to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said: "O King, all our spoils are yours; [divide them among us]. Except for the boys you have chosen from the Children of Israel." He did so, and every man received four youths. Among those youths were Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael, seven thousand from the family of David, eleven thousand from the tribe of Yusuf ibn Ya'qub and his brother Benjamin, eight thousand from the tribe of Asher ibn Ya'qub, fourteen thousand from the tribe of Zebulun ibn Ya'qub, [Naphtali] ibn Ya'qub, four thousand from the tribe of [Judah] ibn Ya'qub, [four] thousand from the tribe of [Reuben and Levi], the two sons of Ya'qub, and whoever remained of the Children of Israel. Bukht Nasr divided them into three groups: a third he left in al-Sham, a third he took captive, and a third he killed.

He took their father to Babylon, and I [sic: the narrator's account] took the ninety thousand boys until I brought them to Babylon. This was the first calamity that Allah sent upon the Children of Israel because of their deeds and their wrongdoing. [[In full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/40–49 and 15/52–45.]] This is the saying of Allah: ﴿So when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might,﴾, meaning Bukht Nasr and his companions.

What is related from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Children of Israel used to recite, and when he reached ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, he wept and his eyes overflowed. Then he closed the mushaf and said: "My Lord, show me this man whom You made the destruction of the Children of Israel at his hands." He was shown in a dream a poor man in Babylon called Bukht Nasr. He set out with wealth [and with a slave of his], and he was a wealthy man. [It was said to him: where are you going?]

He said: "I want to trade." He came to a house in Babylon [and was arrogant] with a god that had no one but him. He began calling the poor and treating them kindly so that no one would come to him. He said: "Is there anyone left among you who is poor?" They said: "Yes, a poor man [who is ill] called Bukht Nasr." He said to his servants: "Go to him." They came to him and he said: "What is your name?" He said: "Bukht Nasr." He said to his servants: "Carry him." They carried him with difficulty, and he treated him until he recovered. He clothed him, gave him provisions, and then the Israelite gave permission to depart. Bukht Nasr wept. The Israelite said: "Why do you weep?" He said: "I weep because you have done to me what you have done, and I have nothing to repay you with." He said: "Yes, a small thing: if you become king, obey me." He [Bukht Nasr] then kept following him in what he asked, and he said: "You are mocking me." What prevented him from giving him what he asked was that he thought he was mocking him in advance. The Israelite said: "You know what prevents you from giving me what I asked, except that Allah wants to carry out what He has decreed and written in His Book, and time has struck its blow."

Sayhur, king of Persia in Babylon, said: "If we send a vanguard to al-Sham..." They said: "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said: "Whom do you think?" They said: "So-and-so." He sent a man and gave him one hundred thousand, and Bukht Nasr went out in his kitchen, not going out except to eat in his kitchen.

When he came to al-Sham, the commander of the vanguard saw the largest part of the land of Allah filled with horses and men. [He came, having been broken], and that weighed on his mind, so he did not ask. He said: Bukht Nasr began to sit in the gatherings of the people of al-Sham, saying: "What prevents you from attacking Babylon? If you attack it, there is nothing beyond its treasury." They said: "We do not know how to fight." He said: "Even if you attacked them?" They said: "We do not know how to fight, and we will not fight until..." He concluded the gatherings of the people of al-Sham. Then they returned, and the vanguard informed their king of what he had seen. Bukht Nasr began saying to the cavalry of the king: "If the king had summoned me, I would have told him something other than what so-and-so told him." This was reported to the king, so he summoned him and informed him of the news and said: "So-and-so, when he saw the largest part of the land of Allah filled with horses and strong men, that grew great in his mind, and he did not ask them about anything." He said: "I did not leave any gathering in al-Sham [...], so I said to them: such and such, and they said to me: such and such."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The commander of the vanguard said to Bukht Nasr: "If you accompany me, I will give you one hundred thousand, and you will desist from what you said." He said: "Even if you gave me the treasury of Babylon, I would not desist." Time struck its blow. Then the king said: "If we send a swift cavalry detachment to al-Sham: if they find an opening, well and good; otherwise they will turn back, and we will have seen what we wanted to see." He said: "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said: "Whom do you think?" They said: "So-and-so." He said: "Is the man who informed me of what he informed me...?" So he summoned Bukht Nasr, sent him, and chose four hundred thousand of their horsemen with him. They set out and ranged through the midst of the lands, [and they took captives] as Allah willed, but they did not [ruin] and did not kill. [Sayhun died, and they said]: "Appoint a successor." They said: "Be patient until your companions come, for they are your horsemen and they will not overturn anything against you. Wait." They waited until Bukht Nasr came [with the captives] and what he had with him, and he divided it among the people. They said: "We have not seen anyone more worthy of kingship than this man," so they made him king. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/39, and the correction of the phrasing from it.]]

Al-Suddi said, with his chain: A man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the ruin of Jerusalem would be the destruction of the Children of Israel. [A boy was sent to me], an orphan, the son of a widow, from the people of Babylon, called Bukht Nasr. They used to be truthful, so he was believed. He began to ask about him until he [came upon his father] while he was gathering firewood. When they came upon him with a bundle of firewood, he threw it down and sat in a corner of the house. He spoke to him and gave him three dirhams. He said: "With this buy food and drink: with one dirham buy meat, with one dirham bread, and with one dirham wine." They ate and drank until the second day, when he did the same to him, and until the third day, when he did the same. Then he said: "I want [you to write me a safe-conduct] if you ever become king one day." He said: "Are you mocking me?" He said: "I am not mocking you, but what is it to you? You will not take [him] as a disciple of mine." Then a sign was spoken to him, and it said: "O king, if it is wealth, it has not diminished anything of yours, so write him a safe-conduct." He said: "What if I come when the people are around you and have come between me and you? Make for me a sign by which you will recognize me." He said: "Raise your document on a reed, and I will recognize you by it." He clothed him and gave him gifts.

Then the king of the Children of Israel used to honor Yahya ibn Zakariya (peace be upon them both), bring him close to his assembly, and consult him about his affairs. He did not decide any matter without him. [He desired] to marry the daughter of a woman he had, so he asked Yahya about that, and Yahya forbade him from marrying her. He said: "I do not find her suitable for you." This reached her mother, and she resented Yahya because he forbade him to marry her daughter. [She went to a young woman] when the king was drinking his wine. She dressed her in thin green garments, perfumed her, adorned her with jewelry, and put over that a black cloak. She sent her to the king and ordered her to give him drink and to present herself to him. If he solicited her, she would refuse until he gave her what she asked. When he gave it to her, she would ask him to bring the head of Yahya ibn Zakariya (peace be upon them both) on a tray. She did so: she kept giving him drink and presenting herself to him. When he had taken from the wine, he solicited her, and she said: "I will not submit until you give me what I ask." He said: "What do you ask?" She said: "I ask you to send for Yahya ibn Zakariya and bring his head to me on this tray." The king said: "Ask me for anything other than this." She said: "I want nothing but this." When she refused him, he sent for him, and his head was brought [and the head was speaking] in the tray when it was placed before him, and it was saying: [It is not lawful for you]. In the morning, his blood was boiling. He ordered dirt to be brought and thrown over it, and it [the blood] pushed the dirt up above. He kept throwing dirt onto it until it reached the wall of the city, and it was still boiling. It reached Sayhabin, and the people were stirred up, and he wanted to send an army against them or to appoint a man over them.

Then Bukht Nasr came to him, spoke with him and said: "The one I sent that time was weak, and I have entered the city and heard the speech of its people. [So send me]." He sent him, and Bukht Nasr set out until, when they reached that place, [they fortified themselves] against him in their cities, and he could not overcome them. When the stay grew hard for them and his companions became hungry, they wished to return. An old woman from among the old women of the Children of Israel came out to him and said: "Where is the commander of the army?" He was brought to her, and she said to him: "It has reached me that you intend [.....] [[an illegible word.]] and then return with your army before you conquer this city." He said: "Yes, my stay has been long and my companions are hungry. I cannot remain beyond what has happened to me." She said: "Tell me, if I open the city for you, will you give me what I ask: that you kill whomever I order you to kill and refrain when I order you to refrain?" He said to her: "Yes." She said: "When morning comes, divide your army into four quarters, then station a quarter at each corner, then raise your hands to heaven and call out: 'We seek victory from You, O Allah, by the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariya,' for it will [collapse]." They did so, and the city collapsed, and they entered from its sides. She said to him: "Withhold your hand and turn to this blood until it calms." She took him to the blood of Yahya while it was on [much dust], and he killed upon it until it calmed. He killed seventy thousand. When the blood had calmed, she said to him: "Withhold your hand, for when Allah the Exalted kills a prophet, He is not satisfied until He kills those who killed him, and those who were pleased with his killing." The owner of the document came to him with a document, and he refrained from them and from the people of his household. He ruined Jerusalem and ordered that carrion be cast into it. He said: "Whoever casts carrion into it, he has his tax for that year." Allah aided him in the ruin of Rome, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya.

When Bukht Nasr ruined it, he took with him the notables and nobles of the Children of Israel. He took Daniel, Ali, Azariah and Mishael; all of these were from the descendants of the prophets. He also took with him the head of Jalut. When he arrived in the land of Babylon, he found that Sayhabin had died, so he became king in his place. The one most honored by him was Daniel and his companions. The Magians envied them for that, so they informed on them to him and said: "Daniel and his companions do not worship your god; they worship another, and they do not eat your slaughtered animals." He summoned them and questioned them. They said: "Indeed, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat from your slaughter." He ordered a trench to be dug for them, and they were cast into it, six of them. He cast a ravenous beast with them to devour them. They did so and went away to eat and drink. Then they came back and found them sitting, and the beast was stretched out with its forelegs between them, not having scratched any of them or harmed any of them in any way. They also found a man with them, so they counted them and found them seven. They said: "What is the matter with this seventh, when there were only six?" The seventh came out to them, and he was an angel. He slapped the beast with a slap so that it went off into the wilds, and Allah transformed it for seven years.

Then Bukht Nasr saw a dream, which Daniel (peace be upon him) interpreted for him. This is what Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim related from Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil, that he heard a monk say: Bukht Nasr saw at the end of his time an idol whose head was of gold, whose chest was of silver, whose belly was of brass, whose thighs were of iron, and whose shins were of clay. Then he saw a stone fall from heaven, which struck it, and then the stone came until it grew and filled what lies between the east and the west. He also saw a tree whose root was in the earth and whose branches were in the sky. Then he saw a man with an axe in his hand, and he heard a caller calling out:

"Strike at its trunk, so that the birds are scattered from its branches, and the beasts and predators are scattered beneath it." And he brought down [....] [[an illegible word.]]

Daniel (peace be upon him) interpreted it for him.

He said: As for the idol you saw: the golden head is you, you are the best of kings. As for the silver chest you saw, your son will reign after you. As for the brass belly you saw, that will come after your son. As for the iron thigh you saw, it is the kingdom of the people of Persia; their kingdom will be harsh like iron. As for the clay leg, the people of Persia will split into two factions, and there will be no stability among them at that time, just as the idol's support did not become firm upon two clay legs. As for the stone that grew until it filled what lies between the east and the west, it is a prophet whom Allah will send at the end of time, and he will break their entire kingdom, and his kingdom will grow until it extends between the east and the west. [[Thus in the original.]]

As for the tree you saw, and the birds upon it, and the predators and beasts beneath it, and what He commanded to be cut down, your kingdom will go; Allah will return you as a bird, the greatest king of birds; then He will return you as a bull, king of beasts; then Allah will return you as a lion, king of predators and wild animals, for seven years. His whole transformation was seven years. In all of that, your heart will be the heart of a man, until you know that ﴿to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, and He is capable over the earth and whoever is upon it. As for the root you saw [standing], [[thus in the original.]] it means your kingdom remains. So Bukht Nasr was transformed into an eagle among birds, a bull among beasts, and a lion among predators. Then Allah returned his kingdom to him, and he became secure and called the people to Allah.

[Wahb ibn Munabbih was asked]: Was he a believer? He said: I found the People of the Book disagreed about him. Some of them said: he died a believer. Others said: he burned the House of Allah and its books, shackled the prophets, and Allah became exceedingly angry with him, so his repentance was not accepted from him at that time.

Al-Tha'labi said, in Al-Jawahir al-Hisan: When Nebuchadnezzar (Bakht Nasr) returned to his form after the transformation, God restored his kingdom to him. Daniel and his companions were the most honored people in his eyes, so the Magians envied them and said to Nebuchadnezzar: "When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating, and that is a disgrace for them." So Nebuchadnezzar prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank. Then he said to the doorkeeper: "Watch for the first one who comes out to you to urinate, and strike him with the tabarzin [the tabarzin: a weapon resembling an axe and a hatchet]. If he says, 'I am Nebuchadnezzar,' say: 'You lie! Nebuchadnezzar commanded me to do this.'" God then withheld urination from Daniel. The first of the people to rise wanting to urinate was Nebuchadnezzar himself, and he was intoxicated; it was night. He got up dragging his garments, and when the doorkeeper saw him he rushed at him, and he said, "I am Nebuchadnezzar." He replied, "You lie! Nebuchadnezzar ordered me to kill the first one who comes out," and he struck him and killed him [in full in Tafsir al-Tabari, with some variation: 15/45].

As for Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, he related something about the destruction of Nebuchadnezzar different from what al-Suddi said. He stated with his chain of narration: When God wished to [......] to send [......] to those who were in [......] [unreadable text], and he was tormenting the Children of Israel, [saying]: "Complete this house which you have ruined, and these people whom you mentioned, who are they, and what is this house?" They said: "This is the House of God and one of His mosques, and these are its people; they were from the [descendants of the prophets], and they wronged [and transgressed] [sic in the original], and disobeyed [their Lord] through their sins. Their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of all creation; He hates them, prevents them, and deprives them [and forbids them]." So when they did what they did, God destroyed them and gave power over them to others.

He said: "Tell me, what will take me up to the highest heaven, so that I may ascend to it, seize those who are in it, and take it as my kingdom, for I have [finished] with the earth and those in it?" They said: "No created being is able to do that." He said: "You will certainly do it [or I will kill you all to the last one]" [sic in the original]. They wept to God and humbled themselves before Him. So God sent against him, by His power, a gnat, to show him his weakness. It entered his nostril, then went out of his nostril and bit into the brain's core, and he could neither rest nor be still until his head was struck upon the core of his brain. When he sensed death, he said to his close family members: "When I die, split open my head and see what it is that has killed me." When he died, his head was split open, and they found the gnat clinging to the core of his brain. This was so that God would show His servants His power and dominion. God also brought back to life those of the Children of Israel who remained in his hands, had mercy upon them, and returned them to Iliya and Syria, where they built, prospered and multiplied until they were in the best state they had ever been.

They claim that God chose the Tawalli of the dead who were killed and joined them. Then, when they returned to Syria, after the Torah had been burnt [and they had no covenant] from God, God renewed their Torah and returned it to them through the tongue of Uzair (peace be upon him). The story has passed. This is all that I have mentioned of the matter of Nebuchadnezzar, according to what has come in the established tafsir concerning the stories of the prophets. However, the narration of those who said that Nebuchadnezzar was the one who attacked the Children of Israel when they [killed] Yahya ibn Zakariyya is an error, according to the people of history (ahl al-siyar), the reports, and the knowledge of the affairs of the past among the People of the Book and the Muslims. This is because they all agree that Nebuchadnezzar attacked the Children of Israel when they killed their prophet Sha'ya (Isaiah), in the time of Uramiya ibn Hilqiya (peace be upon him), and this was the first battle of which God said: "So when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might," meaning Nebuchadnezzar and his armies. They said: From the time of Uramiya and Nebuchadnezzar's destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis until the time of Yahya ibn Zakariyya is four hundred and sixty-one years. This is because they count from the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis by Nebuchadnezzar until its rebuilding in the time of Kusak [so in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 10/220; in al-Tabari: Kirsh] seventy years; then from its rebuilding until Alexander's conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis and his taking of its kingdom until the kingdom of Alexander, eighty-eight years; then from the kingdom of Alexander until the death of Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him), three hundred and sixty-three years, and it is also reported as three hundred and nine years.

The correct account of this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned. He said: Many [sins] occurred among the Children of Israel after Syria had been rebuilt and they had returned to it after Nebuchadnezzar's destruction of it and his taking them captive from it. Afterwards they began to commit misdeeds after the death of Uzair (peace be upon him), and God forgave them. God sent prophets among them, and a group they called liars and a group they killed, until the last of the prophets God sent among them were Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa, and they were from the house of Dawud. Zakariyya died, and Yahya was killed because of the king's desire to marry his niece, according to the saying of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr; his niece according to al-Suddi; and his brother's daughter according to Ibn Abbas.

This is the most correct, God willing, as related by al-A'mash from al-Minhal from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Isa son of Maryam and Yahya ibn Zakariyya were sent with twelve disciples to teach people, and among what they forbade was marriage to a brother's daughter. He said: The king had a niece who pleased him, and he wanted to marry her; she had a need that she asked of him every day. He mentioned the hadith in full concerning the killing of Yahya [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/219].

Returning to the hadith of Ibn Ishaq: when God raised Musa from among them, and they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya, some people say they killed Zakariyya, a king of Babylon named Khardus rose against them, marching with the people of Babylon until he entered Syria against them. When he prevailed over them, he ordered one of the heads of his armies, called [Nabur Zadhan], who was in charge of killing, and said to him: "I had sworn by my god that if I prevailed over the people of Bayt al-Maqdis I would kill them until their blood flowed in the middle of my camp, but I do not find anyone to kill," and he ordered him to kill them until Nabur Zadhan had accomplished that. He entered Bayt al-Maqdis, and in the place where they used to offer their sacrifices he [found blood boiling]. He asked them about it. They said: "This is the blood of a sacrifice we offered, and it was not accepted from us, so that is why it boils as you see. We have offered sacrifices for eight hundred years, and they were accepted from us except this one." He said: "You have not told me the truth." They said to him: "If it were as in the first of our times, it would have been accepted from us, but kingship, prophethood and revelation have ceased among us, so it was not accepted." So Nabur Zadhan slaughtered seven hundred and seventy of their chiefs upon that blood, but it did not settle. He then ordered seven thousand of their followers and their wives to be slaughtered upon the blood [sic in the original], but it did not return nor settle. When Nabur Zadhan saw that the blood would not settle, he said to them: "Woe to you, O Children of Israel! Be truthful with me and be patient in the matter of your Lord, [for you have ruled long] upon the earth, doing in it whatever you wished, before I leave no blower of fire, neither female nor male, but I kill him." When [they saw the hardship] and the severity of the killing, they told him the truth, saying: "This is the blood of a prophet from among us who used to forbid us from many things that anger God. If we had obeyed him in them, it would have been better for us. He used to inform us of the kingdom, but we did not believe him, so we killed him." Nabur Zadhan said to them: "What was his name?" He said: "Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said: "Did you believe me? For such a thing your Lord takes vengeance upon you." When Nabur Zadhan saw that they had believed him, he fell down prostrate and said to those around him: "Close the gates of the city, and gather whoever is here of Khardus's army, and leave the Children of Israel." He said: "O Yahya ibn Zakariyya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, and what has been killed of them because of you. Be still by God's leave before none of your people remain." So the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya settled by God's leave, and Nabur Zadhan lifted the killing from them [and said: "I have believed in what the Children of Israel believed, and I have affirmed it and am certain that there is no lord but Him. If there were another with Him, it would not be right; if He had a partner, the heavens and the earth would not hold; if He had a son, it would not be right. Blessed and sanctified is He, glorified and magnified, the King of kings, to whom belongs the kingdom of the seven heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them, and He is over all things Powerful. To Him belong judgment, knowledge, might and majesty. He it is who spread out the earth and cast into it firm mountains lest it should shake; likewise it befits my Lord to be, and His dominion is so"] [see Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/55]. Then God revealed to some of the leaders of the remaining prophets that Nabur Zadhan was "Hibbur" [the Hibbur in Hebrew means: the narration of faith], a truthful one.

And Nabur Zadhan said to the Children of Israel: "O Children of Israel, the enemy of God, Khardus, has commanded me to kill among you until your blood flows in the middle of his army, and I am not able to disobey him." They said to him: "Do what you have been commanded." So he ordered them to dig a trench, and he ordered their livestock—horses, mules, donkeys, camels, cattle and sheep—to be brought, and he slaughtered them until the blood flowed through the army. He ordered the corpses of those killed earlier to be cast upon the slaughtered animals until they were on top of them. Khardus thought only that what was in the trench was of the Children of Israel. When the blood reached his army, he sent to Nabur Zadhan: "Lift the killing from them, for I have heard of their blood, and I have taken vengeance upon them for what they did" [see Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/55]. Then he departed from them to Babylon, having destroyed the Children of Israel or nearly so. This is the last battle which God sent against the Children of Israel in His words: "And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will certainly cause corruption in the earth twice..." and so on.

The first battle was Nebuchadnezzar and his armies; then God returned the turn of victory to them. The last battle was Khardus and his armies, and [.....] after that [.....]. Thus the kingship in Syria and its regions passed to the Romans and the Greeks. Then the Children of Israel multiplied and spread again, and they had at Bayt al-Maqdis [.....] not in the manner of kingship, and they were in readiness and strength until they changed, introduced innovations, violated the sacred prohibitions and committed the prescribed punishments. So God gave power over them to Titus son of Sibanu the Roman, who ruined their lands, drove them out, and God removed from them kingship and leadership and imposed humiliation upon them. There is no nation among the nations except that they are under [humiliation], while kingship is with others. Bayt al-Maqdis remained in ruin until the days of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him), when the Muslims rebuilt it by his command.

Abu 'Awana related from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the words of God: "And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book..." the verses. He said: As for those who "searched through the homes" (fajasu khilal al-diyar), it was Marhab al-Jazari; when he reached His words "a destruction" (tatbiran), it was Jalut al-Jazari, a branch of [.....] [unreadable text].

Then he said: "Then We gave you back the return against them..." up to "a destruction." He said: This is Bakht Nasr, who ruined Bayt al-Maqdis.

Then He said to them after that: "It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you [on this then]" [sic in the original], "but if you return, We will return," He said: They returned, so they were overpowered again, and God sent against them the king of the Romans; then they returned again and were overpowered again, and God sent against them the king of [......] [unreadable word]; then they returned again and were overpowered again by Sabur Dhu al-Aktaf.

Qatada on this verse, "And We decreed" (wa qadayna): He decreed upon the people as you hear. In the first, He sent Jalut against them, who took captives, killed, ruined, and "searched through the homes"... "Then We gave you back the return against them" — i.e., O Children of Israel — "the return," and kingship in the time of Dawud (peace be upon him). "So when the promise of the Hereafter came" — the last of the two returns — God sent against them Bakht Nasr, the most hated of God's creation, who took captives, killed, ruined Bayt al-Maqdis, and gave them the torment of humiliation. Then He said: "It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you" [sic in the original], so God returned to them with His mercy, then they returned to what He tormented them for, so God sent against them whatever He willed of His calamity and punishment. Then God sent against them this tribe of the Arabs, as He said: "And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with the worst torment" [Surah al-A'raf: 167] [.....] [unreadable text].

"And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book": i.e., We informed them and made them know in what We gave them of the Books.

Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: it means "And We decreed against you," and on this interpretation "ila" (to) means "ala" (upon), and "al-Kitab" means the Preserved Tablet. "You will certainly cause corruption": it was said the lam is the lam of oath: "By God, you will certainly cause corruption in the earth twice," through sins, "and you will certainly exalt yourselves, and you will certainly wrong people with great arrogance." "So when the promise of the first of them came," meaning the first of the two times, and they differed concerning it. According to Qatada's view, their corruption in the first time was that they opposed the rulings of the Torah, [judged] their Lord, did not preserve the command of their prophet Musa (peace be upon him), committed the prohibitions and transgressed against people.

Al-Suddi said, in a report he related from Abu Malik and Abu Jahl from Ibn Abbas and from Umayya al-Hamadhani from Ibn Mas'ud: the first of the two corruptions was the killing of Zakariyya.

Ibn Ishaq said: their corruption in the first time was their killing of Sha'ya ibn Amsiya in the time of Irmiya in the tree.

Ibn Ishaq also said: some people of knowledge informed him that Zakariyya died a natural death and was not killed, and that the one killed was Sha'ya (peace be upon him).

"We sent against you servants of Ours": meaning Jalut al-Jazari and his armies, and he is the one whom Dawud killed.

Qatada said, and it is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas; Abu al-Mu'alla and Ya'la [sic in the original] said from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they were Saharib from the people of Nineveh, which is Mosul. Abu Bishr said from him: Sarkhan al-Khazri; and Ibn Ishaq said: Bakht Nasr al-Babili and his companions.

"Of great might": meaning strength; "in war" (shadid): "so they searched through" — i.e., they feared and roamed about.

Ibn Abbas said: they walked about. Al-Farra': they killed you among your homes.

He recited a verse of Hassan:
"And among us is the one who met with the sword of Muhammad, and the enemies were searched through by him, the breadth of the armies."

Abu 'Ubayda: they sought what was in them, as a man searches for news, meaning he seeks it. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/216.]

Al-Qutayba: [they lived and killed] and corrupted. [See Zad al-Masir by Ibn al-Jawzi: 5/8, and he attributed it to Abu Abd al-Rahman.]

Ibn Jarir: they went about the homes seeking them and killing them, going and coming; so he combined the interpretations.

Ibn Abbas recited "fa-hasu" with the letter ha', and its meaning is the same.

"Between the homes" (khilal al-diyar). "And it was a promise fulfilled": a decree that is certain, with no breaking of it. "Then We gave you back the return": the turn and the dominion "against them," "and We aided you with wealth and sons, and made you more numerous in manpower" (nafiran): in number.

Al-Qutayba said: the nafir is from "nafara" with a man from his clan and household; it is said "al-nafir" and "al-nafir" (the one who goes forth), and its root is like "al-qadir" and "al-qadir" (the capable one).

"If you do good" — O Children of Israel — "you do good for yourselves": for it is a reward and its benefit; "and if you do evil, then it is for them" (fa-laha), i.e., against them, like His words "Peace be upon you" (fa-salamun laka), i.e., upon you.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: He said it as in "because your Lord has inspired to her" (bi-anna rabbaka awha laha), i.e., to her. It was also said: "fa-laha" means the reward and the punishment.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it means "fa-laha" — a Lord who forgives evil. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/217.]

"So when the promise of the Hereafter came" — i.e., the last time of your corruption; this is according to their intention to kill Isa (peace be upon him) when he was raised, and their killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him). So God gave power over them to the Persians and the Romans [.....] [unreadable text]; they killed them, took them captive, expelled them from their lands, and seized their lands and wealth. That is His words: "to sadden your faces" — i.e., to grieve you. The readers differed concerning it.

Al-Kisa'i read "linasu'a" with the nun and an opened hamza, as glorification, considering the speaker as "We," as in "wa qadayna," "wa ba'athna," "wa radadna," "wa amdadna," "wa ja'alna." This was also narrated from Ali (may God be pleased with him).

In confirmation of this reading, Ubayy ibn Ka'b read: "Linasu'anna wujuhakum," with the nun and the emphatic particle.

The people of Kufa read with the ya' in the singular: it has two possible meanings: one is "liyasu'a Allah wujuhakum" (that God may sadden your faces); the second is "liyasu'a [al-'aduw] wujuhakum" (that the enemy may sadden your faces).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 4–8 (part 4 of 4):

Others recited: ﴿لِيَسُوؤُا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ with the ya' and with the hamza vowelled with a damma, in the plural (jam'), meaning: the servants will make your faces ill-treated, [as for] "those possessing great might" (ﷺ... ) your faces. ﴿وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis and its surroundings, ﴿كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ as they entered it the first time. ﴿وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا﴾ and that they may destroy, or that they may annihilate, ﴿مَا عَلَوْا﴾ what they had overpowered; they overcame it. ﴿تَتْبِيراً﴾ [with] destruction. ﴿عَسى﴾ perhaps, meaning ﴿لعلّ﴾: ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾, O Children of Israel, ﴿أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ﴾ may have mercy upon you after their vengeance against you. ﴿وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنا﴾ And if you return, We shall return.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ﴾ if you return to disobedience, ﴿عُدْنا﴾ We shall return to punishment. So they returned, and Allah sent against them Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they gave the jizya ﴿عَنْ يَدٍ وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ﴾ [from their own hand] while they were humbled. ... ﴿وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيراً﴾ "a prison" (ma'an): a confinement and a place of detention, from al-hasr, which is confinement. The Arabs call the palm grove (al-nakhil) ḥaṣūr, and the king ḥaṣīr, [because he is veiled and confined] [[as in the original.]] from the people.

Labid said:
"And tall men who overpower necks, as if they were jinn standing at the gate of the ḥaṣīr"
meaning the gate of the king. From this comes: "inḥaṣara fi al-kalām" when he is held back in speech and unable to continue, and "al-rajul al-ḥaṣūr" (a man restrained from women), and "ḥaṣara al-ghā'iṭ" (he was constipated).

Al-Hasan said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيراً﴾ meaning a bedding and a cushion; he took it to mean the ḥaṣīr that is spread out, since the Arabs call a small carpet ḥaṣīr. This is a good interpretation and a sound explanation.

And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book... up to His words ﴿and a prison﴾.

Sufyan ibn Suhayl narrated from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel transgressed, became arrogant, and killed the prophets, God sent against them the king of Persia, Bukht Nasr. God had given him dominion for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), besieged it, and conquered it. He killed seventy thousand in retribution for the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him). Then he took its people captive, stripped Bayt al-Maqdis of its ornaments, and extracted seventy thousand and one hundred ornamented chariots [until he brought them to Babylon]." [[From the Tafsir of al-Tabari: 15/29.]]

Hudhayfah said: "O Messenger of God, Bayt al-Maqdis must have been great in God's sight." He said: "Indeed. Sulayman ibn Dawud built it of gold, rubies, and chrysolite. Its flagstones were of gold, its paving was of silver, and its paving was of gold. God gave him that and subjected the devils to him, so they brought these things to him in the blink of an eye. Then Bukht Nasr carried these things away until he reached Babylon. The Children of Israel remained under his hand for one hundred years, and the Magians and the sons of Magians enslaved them, though they were prophets and the sons of prophets. Then God, exalted is He, had mercy on them and revealed to a king of the Persians named Kurush, who was a believer, that he should march against the remnants of the Children of Israel so as to rescue them. Kurush took the Children of Israel captive and the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, until he returned them to it. The Children of Israel then remained obedient to God for one hundred years. Then they returned to sin, so God empowered against them a king called Antiyakhush. He raided the Children of Israel and brought them to Bayt al-Maqdis, took its people captive, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis. He said to them: 'O Children of Israel, if you return to sin, we will return against you with captivity.' They returned to sin, so God empowered against them a Roman king called Maqsir ibn Isbiyanus. He raided them by land and sea, took them captive, seized the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is the description of the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis. The Mahdi (the rightly guided one) will return them to Bayt al-Maqdis. They are one thousand and seven hundred ships, which will be sent onto Yafa until they are transported to Bayt al-Maqdis, carried by its (the ships') hands. God will gather the first and the last." [20] [[See the Tafsir of al-Tabari: 15/29-30.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Among what God revealed to Musa concerning the report of the Children of Israel, regarding their events and what they would do after him, was: ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel...﴾ up to His words ﴿and a prison﴾. The Children of Israel had among them young men and sins, and God, in that, was forgiving toward them, compassionate to them, and benevolent to them. The first thing that befell them, because of their sins, from those events, was as He informed through the tongue of Musa (peace be upon him): that a king among them called Siddiqah... God, exalted and majestic is He, whenever a king ruled over them, would send a prophet to strengthen and guide them, and who would be between him and God, Exalted is He. He would speak to them about their affairs, for the Books were revealed to them. They were commanded only to follow the Torah and the rulings in it, and were forbidden from disobedience, and were called to what they had abandoned of obedience. When God gave that king dominion, God sent Sha'iya ibn Amsiya, and that was before the mission of Zakariyya, Yahya, and 'Isa. Sha'iya is the one who gave glad tidings of 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: "Rejoice [...] [[An illegible word.]] Now there will come to you a rider on a donkey, and after him a rider on a camel." That king ruled over the Children of Israel and Bayt al-Maqdis for a time. When his reign ended, the events grew severe, and Sha'iya was with them. God sent against them Sanharib, king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He advanced until he came around Bayt al-Maqdis, while the king was ill with an ulcer on his leg. Sha'iya came to him and said: "O king of the Children of Israel, Sanharib, king of Babylon, has descended with his armies, six hundred thousand strong. People have been terrified of them and have scattered from them." This weighed heavily on the king, and he said: "O Prophet of God, has a revelation from God come to you concerning what has happened, so that you may tell us how God will deal with us and with Sanharib and his armies?"

The prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: "No revelation has come." While they were in that state, God, exalted is He, revealed to Sha'iya the prophet (peace be upon him): "Go to the king of the Children of Israel and command him to make his testament and to appoint over his kingdom whomever he wishes from his household, for he is dying." Sha'iya came to Siddiqah and said: "Your Lord has revealed to you that He commands you to make your testament and to appoint whomever you wish over your kingdom from your household, for you are dying." When Sha'iya said this to Siddiqah, he turned toward the qiblah, prayed, supplicated, and wept. He said while praying and humbling himself before God, Exalted is He, with a sincere, reliant, steadfast heart and a true conviction: "O God, Lord of lords, God of gods, the Holy, the Most Holy, O Merciful, O Compassionate, O Kind, who is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep, You honored me through my deed and my action, and through my good judgment over the Children of Israel. All of that was from You, and You know it better than I do, in my secret and in my open conduct." And the Merciful accepted his supplication, for he was a righteous servant. God revealed to Sha'iya and commanded him to inform the king Siddiqah that his Lord had answered him, accepted from him, had mercy on him, and had postponed his term by fifteen years, and that He would deliver him from his enemy Sanharib, king of Babylon, and his armies. Sha'iya the prophet (peace be upon him) came to him and informed him of that. When he said this, the pain left him, the grief departed from him, and he fell prostrate and said: "O my God and God of my fathers, to You I prostrate, to You I glorify, to You I magnify and exalt. You are the One who gives dominion to whom You will and removes dominion from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will and abase whom You will, ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible﴾. You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. You answer the supplication of the distressed. You are the One who answered my supplication and had mercy on my affliction." When he raised his head, God revealed to Sha'iya: "Tell the king Siddiqah to command one of his servants to bring figs, place them on his ulcer, and he will be healed and become strong again." He did so, and was healed. The king said to Sha'iya: "Ask your Lord to give us a sign of what He will do to this enemy of ours."

God said to Sha'iya: "Tell him that I have sufficed you against your enemy, delivered you from them, and that they will all become dead, except Sanharib and five of his scribes."

When they awoke in the morning, a crier came and shouted at the gate of the city: "O king of the Children of Israel, God has sufficed you against your enemy. Come out, for Sanharib and those with him have perished." When the king came out, he sought Sanharib but did not find him among the dead. The king sent men in pursuit of him, and they caught up with him in a desert, with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukht Nasr. They put them in shackles and brought them to the king of the Children of Israel. When they saw them, he fell prostrate from sunrise until the afternoon prayer. Then he said to Sanharib: "How do you see what our Lord has done to you? Did we not kill you by His power and might, while you and we were heedless?" Sanharib said: "The news of your Lord and His victory over you, and His mercy with which He showed you mercy, has reached me before I left your land. But I did not obey a guide, and nothing brought me to wretchedness except the weakness of my mind. Had I listened and obeyed, I would not have fought you. But wretchedness overcame me and those with me." Siddiqah said: "Praise be to God, Lord of might, who [has spared you] by what He willed to leave of you and those with you, for the honor He holds for you. He left you and those with you only so that they might increase in wretchedness in this world and in punishment in the Hereafter, and so that you might inform those behind you of what you have seen of our Lord's action. Therefore, you and those with you are [to be] brought before God for the blood of a tick, even if you were killed." Then the king of the Children of Israel ordered the commander of his army to put shackles on their necks, and they were paraded seventy times around Bayt al-Maqdis [and Amiya] [[A town in the region of Greater Syria.]]. He provided for them each day with two loaves of barley for each man.

Sanharib said to the king of the Children of Israel: "Death is better than what is being done to us, so do what you have commanded." The king ordered them taken to a prison of execution. God revealed to the prophet Sha'iya (peace be upon him): "Tell the king of the Children of Israel to release Sanharib and those with him, so that they may warn those behind them, and to honor them and carry them until they reach their land." Shay'a [for the king, that] was conveyed, and he did it. Sanharib and those with him set out and arrived at Babylon. When they arrived, he gathered the people and informed them how God had dealt with his armies. His soothsayers and sorcerers said to him: "O king of [Babylon] [[An addition from the Tafsir of al-Tabari: 15/32.]], we used to relate to you the news of their Lord, the news of their prophet, and God's revelation to their prophet, but you did not obey us. This is a people whom no one can withstand, with their Lord." The matter of Sanharib was among what they had feared. Then God spared them from him, as a reminder and a lesson. Sanharib then remained for seven years and died. He was succeeded by his grandson, who continued in the same way, and he governed them as his grandfather had, and ruled until some of them killed others [among themselves]. Their prophet Sha'iya was among them, not submitting to him and not accepting from him. When they did that, God said to Sha'iya: "Stand among your people, and I will reveal through your tongue."

When the prophet (peace be upon him) stood up, God loosened his tongue with revelation, and he said: "O heaven, listen; O earth, be silent..." up to the end, for God wishes to recount the affair of the Children of Israel, whom He reared with favor, chose for Himself, singled out with His honor, preferred over His servants, and welcomed with generosity. They were like lost sheep without a shepherd. He gave refuge to their strayed ones, gathered their lost ones, mended their broken ones, healed their sick ones, fattened their emaciated ones, and guarded their fat ones. But when He had done that, they became insolent, and their rams butted one another until they killed one another, so that no sound bone remained to which a broken one could be set. Woe to this sinful people, who do not know from where good has come to them. Indeed, the far-off one is one who remembers his homeland and returns to it. The donkey is one who remembers the stable where he was fed, and returns to it. The ox is one who remembers the pasture where he grew fat, and returns to it. But these people do not know from where good has come to them, while they are people of understanding and intellect, not cattle or donkeys. I shall strike a parable for them, so let them listen. Say to them: "How do you see a land that was empty for a time, ruined, dead, with no habitation in it, and which had a wise and mighty Lord? He turned to it with cultivation, and disliked that His land should be ruined. He surrounded it with a wall, built a palace in it, dug a river, planted in it grafts of olive, pomegranate, date palm, grape, and all kinds of fruit. He entrusted it to a guardian of judgment, resolve, and ambition, a vigilant, strong, trustworthy keeper, and waited for it. When it bore its fruit, its blossom produced carobs." They said: "Evil is this land. We see that its wall should be demolished, its palaces, its river buried, its keeper seized, and its grafts burned, until it becomes as it was at first: ruined, dead, with no habitation in it."

God said to them: "As for the wall, it is My covenant. As for the palace, it is My law. As for the river, it is My Book. As for the keeper, he is My prophet. As for the grafts, they are My people. As for the carob that the grafts produced, it is their evil deeds. I have already decreed against them the decree they brought upon themselves. They are a parable that God has struck for them. They draw near to Me by slaughtering cows and sheep, yet meat does not reach Me nor do I eat it. They claim to draw near to Me by piety and by refraining from slaying the souls that I have forbidden, yet their hands are dyed with it and their garments are soaked with its blood. They build houses for Me as mosques and purify their interiors, while they defile their hearts and bodies and soil them. What need have I of building houses when I do not dwell in them? And what need have I of adorning mosques when I do not enter them? I only commanded that they be raised so that I may be remembered in them and glorified, and to be a sign for whoever wishes to pray in them. They say: 'If God were able to unite our hearts, He would unite them. If God were able to give understanding to our hearts, He would give them understanding.' So go and take two dry twigs, then go to them and call them, in their most gathered gathering, and say to the twigs: 'God commands you to become one twig.' It was done. In that very session they became mixed and became one. Then God said to them: 'I have indeed been able to give understanding to dry twigs and to make them agree with each other. So how could I not be able to unite your hearts, if I wish? Or how could I not be able to give understanding to their hearts, when I am the One who fashioned them?'

They say: 'We fasted, but our fasting was not raised. We prayed, but our prayer was not accepted. We gave charity, but our charities were not purified. We called upon Him like the cooing of doves, and wept like the howling of wolves, yet we are not heard and we are not answered.' God said: 'Ask them what prevents Me from responding to them. Do I not hear the listeners, see the watchers, come nearest to those who answer, and have the most mercy of the merciful? Has My hand now become withered?'

I say: How could it be, when My hands are extended with goodness? I spend as I will, and the keys of the treasuries are with Me; none opens them but Me. Or is it that My mercy has become constricted? How could it be, when My mercy has encompassed everything, and the merciful show mercy only by its bounty? Or is it that [stinginess has overtaken Me]? Or am I not the most generous of the generous and the Opener of good things? I am the most bountiful of givers and the most honorable of those who are asked. If these people had looked at themselves with the wisdom that was illuminated in their hearts, and had not cast it aside and bartered it for this world, they would have seen from where they came, and they would have been certain that their own souls are the greatest of their enemies. So how should I raise their fasting when they clothe it with false speech, and strengthen themselves by it with the sustenance of the unlawful? How should I make their prayer radiant when their hearts incline toward one who wars against Me and violates My sanctities? Or how should their charities be purified with Me, when they give in charity from other people's wealth, and I only reward its rightful owners who were wronged? Or how should I answer their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues, while their deeds are far from it? I answer only the one who calls with gentleness, and I hear the words of the weak and the poor. Indeed, among the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. If they had shown mercy to the poor, drawn near to the weak, given justice to the oppressed, supported the wronged and the defeated, done justice to the absent, and rendered to the orphan, the widow, the needy, and every possessor of a right his right, then, were it fitting for Me to speak to humankind, I would have spoken to them. I would have been the light of their sight, the hearing of their ears, the understanding of their hearts, I would have strengthened their supports, and been the strength of their hands and feet. And their tongues and minds would have been strengthened."

They say, when they heard my words and my messages reached them: "These are fabricated sayings, traditions handed down, and a composition like the composition of sorcerers and soothsayers." They claimed that if they wished, they could bring a discourse like it, and that they could attain knowledge of the unseen. They would be informed by what the devils reveal to them, and they would speak to them, and what is said and kept secret would be hidden. And they would be doing this while I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal. I have decreed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, a decree which I have made binding upon Myself, and I have set beyond it a determined term that will inevitably come to pass. If they truly believe in what they claim of the knowledge of the unseen, then let them inform you when I will execute it, or at what time it will occur. And if they are able to bring about whatever they wish, then let them bring the like of the power by which I have executed it. For I shall make it manifest over all religion, ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verses 4–8 (part 2 of 4):

And if they are able to say whatever they wish, then let them produce the like of the wisdom with which I govern this affair of decree, if you are truthful. For I decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth that I would place prophethood among the lowly, sovereignty in supplication, honor among the abased, strength among the weak, wealth among the poor, abundance among the few, [cities in the wastelands], thickets in the sands, the ... in the pastures, knowledge among the ignorant and judgment among the unlettered. So ask them: when is this, who will uphold it, at whose hand will it be established, and who are the helpers and supporters of this matter, if they know? Indeed, I shall send forth for this a prophet, a non-blind man among the blind and not a misguided one among the misguided. He is neither harsh nor coarse, [nor loud-voiced in the markets], [nor adorned with obscenity], nor one who speaks foul speech. I shall guide him to every good thing. I shall grant him every [noble] character. I shall make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, pardon and kindness his character, justice and kindness his conduct, truth his law, guidance his leader, Islam his creed, and Ahmad his name. Through him I shall guide after misguidance, teach after ignorance, raise up after [abasement], make known after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and bring together hearts that differ, desires that scatter, and nations that are dispersed. I shall make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, out of faith in Me, monotheism for Me, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray to Me standing, sitting, bowing and prostrating. They will fight in My cause in rows and waves, and they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I shall inspire them with glorification, monotheism, praise, commendation and exaltation of Me in their mosques, their gatherings, their beds, their comings and goings, and their dwelling places. They will proclaim My greatness, declare My oneness and sanctify Me in the marketplaces. They will purify for Me their faces and their extremities, and they will tie their garments at the ends. Their offering is their blood, their Gospels are in their chests, they are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I give to whom I will, and Allah is the Owner of great bounty.

When their prophet Sha'ya had finished his address to them, they rushed upon him to kill him, and he fled from them. A tree met him and split open for him, and he entered it. [Satan came upon him in the tree], and he seized the hem of his garment and showed it to them. They placed the saw in its middle and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle. [Allah appointed] over the Children of Israel, after they killed Sha'ya, a man from among them called Nashiyah ibn Amus. And He sent al-Khadir as a prophet to them. The name of al-Khadir is Irmiya ibn Hilqiya, and he was from the tribe of Harun ibn Imran. He was called al-Khadir because he sat upon a white patch of land and it [trembled and became green] when he rose from it. Allah said to Irmiya when He sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel: "O Irmiya, before I created you I chose you, and before I formed you in your mother's womb I sanctified you, and before I brought you out from your mother's womb I purified you." The hadith is mentioned in full, including Irmiya's sermon to his people and the fatwa he issued, and the entry of Bukht Nasr and his armies into Jerusalem, and his trampling of al-Sham, as we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.

When Irmiya saw that, he flew away until he mingled with the wild beasts. Bukht Nasr and his armies entered Jerusalem, trampled al-Sham, killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them, and ruined Jerusalem. Then he ordered his soldiers that each man should fill his waterskin with dirt and throw it into Jerusalem, and they threw dirt into it until they filled it. Then he returned to the land of Babylon, taking with him the captives of the Children of Israel. He ordered them to gather everyone who was in Jerusalem, so they gathered before him every young and old person of the Children of Israel, and he chose from them seventy thousand boys.

When the spoils of his army were brought out and he wished to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said: "O King, all our spoils are yours; [divide them among us]. Except for the boys you have chosen from the Children of Israel." He did so, and every man received four youths. Among those youths were Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael, seven thousand from the family of David, eleven thousand from the tribe of Yusuf ibn Ya'qub and his brother Benjamin, eight thousand from the tribe of Asher ibn Ya'qub, fourteen thousand from the tribe of Zebulun ibn Ya'qub, [Naphtali] ibn Ya'qub, four thousand from the tribe of [Judah] ibn Ya'qub, [four] thousand from the tribe of [Reuben and Levi], the two sons of Ya'qub, and whoever remained of the Children of Israel. Bukht Nasr divided them into three groups: a third he left in al-Sham, a third he took captive, and a third he killed.

He took their father to Babylon, and I [sic: the narrator's account] took the ninety thousand boys until I brought them to Babylon. This was the first calamity that Allah sent upon the Children of Israel because of their deeds and their wrongdoing. [[In full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/40–49 and 15/52–45.]] This is the saying of Allah: ﴿So when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might,﴾, meaning Bukht Nasr and his companions.

What is related from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Children of Israel used to recite, and when he reached ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, he wept and his eyes overflowed. Then he closed the mushaf and said: "My Lord, show me this man whom You made the destruction of the Children of Israel at his hands." He was shown in a dream a poor man in Babylon called Bukht Nasr. He set out with wealth [and with a slave of his], and he was a wealthy man. [It was said to him: where are you going?]

He said: "I want to trade." He came to a house in Babylon [and was arrogant] with a god that had no one but him. He began calling the poor and treating them kindly so that no one would come to him. He said: "Is there anyone left among you who is poor?" They said: "Yes, a poor man [who is ill] called Bukht Nasr." He said to his servants: "Go to him." They came to him and he said: "What is your name?" He said: "Bukht Nasr." He said to his servants: "Carry him." They carried him with difficulty, and he treated him until he recovered. He clothed him, gave him provisions, and then the Israelite gave permission to depart. Bukht Nasr wept. The Israelite said: "Why do you weep?" He said: "I weep because you have done to me what you have done, and I have nothing to repay you with." He said: "Yes, a small thing: if you become king, obey me." He [Bukht Nasr] then kept following him in what he asked, and he said: "You are mocking me." What prevented him from giving him what he asked was that he thought he was mocking him in advance. The Israelite said: "You know what prevents you from giving me what I asked, except that Allah wants to carry out what He has decreed and written in His Book, and time has struck its blow."

Sayhur, king of Persia in Babylon, said: "If we send a vanguard to al-Sham..." They said: "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said: "Whom do you think?" They said: "So-and-so." He sent a man and gave him one hundred thousand, and Bukht Nasr went out in his kitchen, not going out except to eat in his kitchen.

When he came to al-Sham, the commander of the vanguard saw the largest part of the land of Allah filled with horses and men. [He came, having been broken], and that weighed on his mind, so he did not ask. He said: Bukht Nasr began to sit in the gatherings of the people of al-Sham, saying: "What prevents you from attacking Babylon? If you attack it, there is nothing beyond its treasury." They said: "We do not know how to fight." He said: "Even if you attacked them?" They said: "We do not know how to fight, and we will not fight until..." He concluded the gatherings of the people of al-Sham. Then they returned, and the vanguard informed their king of what he had seen. Bukht Nasr began saying to the cavalry of the king: "If the king had summoned me, I would have told him something other than what so-and-so told him." This was reported to the king, so he summoned him and informed him of the news and said: "So-and-so, when he saw the largest part of the land of Allah filled with horses and strong men, that grew great in his mind, and he did not ask them about anything." He said: "I did not leave any gathering in al-Sham [...], so I said to them: such and such, and they said to me: such and such."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The commander of the vanguard said to Bukht Nasr: "If you accompany me, I will give you one hundred thousand, and you will desist from what you said." He said: "Even if you gave me the treasury of Babylon, I would not desist." Time struck its blow. Then the king said: "If we send a swift cavalry detachment to al-Sham: if they find an opening, well and good; otherwise they will turn back, and we will have seen what we wanted to see." He said: "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said: "Whom do you think?" They said: "So-and-so." He said: "Is the man who informed me of what he informed me...?" So he summoned Bukht Nasr, sent him, and chose four hundred thousand of their horsemen with him. They set out and ranged through the midst of the lands, [and they took captives] as Allah willed, but they did not [ruin] and did not kill. [Sayhun died, and they said]: "Appoint a successor." They said: "Be patient until your companions come, for they are your horsemen and they will not overturn anything against you. Wait." They waited until Bukht Nasr came [with the captives] and what he had with him, and he divided it among the people. They said: "We have not seen anyone more worthy of kingship than this man," so they made him king. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/39, and the correction of the phrasing from it.]]

Al-Suddi said, with his chain: A man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the ruin of Jerusalem would be the destruction of the Children of Israel. [A boy was sent to me], an orphan, the son of a widow, from the people of Babylon, called Bukht Nasr. They used to be truthful, so he was believed. He began to ask about him until he [came upon his father] while he was gathering firewood. When they came upon him with a bundle of firewood, he threw it down and sat in a corner of the house. He spoke to him and gave him three dirhams. He said: "With this buy food and drink: with one dirham buy meat, with one dirham bread, and with one dirham wine." They ate and drank until the second day, when he did the same to him, and until the third day, when he did the same. Then he said: "I want [you to write me a safe-conduct] if you ever become king one day." He said: "Are you mocking me?" He said: "I am not mocking you, but what is it to you? You will not take [him] as a disciple of mine." Then a sign was spoken to him, and it said: "O king, if it is wealth, it has not diminished anything of yours, so write him a safe-conduct." He said: "What if I come when the people are around you and have come between me and you? Make for me a sign by which you will recognize me." He said: "Raise your document on a reed, and I will recognize you by it." He clothed him and gave him gifts.

Then the king of the Children of Israel used to honor Yahya ibn Zakariya (peace be upon them both), bring him close to his assembly, and consult him about his affairs. He did not decide any matter without him. [He desired] to marry the daughter of a woman he had, so he asked Yahya about that, and Yahya forbade him from marrying her. He said: "I do not find her suitable for you." This reached her mother, and she resented Yahya because he forbade him to marry her daughter. [She went to a young woman] when the king was drinking his wine. She dressed her in thin green garments, perfumed her, adorned her with jewelry, and put over that a black cloak. She sent her to the king and ordered her to give him drink and to present herself to him. If he solicited her, she would refuse until he gave her what she asked. When he gave it to her, she would ask him to bring the head of Yahya ibn Zakariya (peace be upon them both) on a tray. She did so: she kept giving him drink and presenting herself to him. When he had taken from the wine, he solicited her, and she said: "I will not submit until you give me what I ask." He said: "What do you ask?" She said: "I ask you to send for Yahya ibn Zakariya and bring his head to me on this tray." The king said: "Ask me for anything other than this." She said: "I want nothing but this." When she refused him, he sent for him, and his head was brought [and the head was speaking] in the tray when it was placed before him, and it was saying: [It is not lawful for you]. In the morning, his blood was boiling. He ordered dirt to be brought and thrown over it, and it [the blood] pushed the dirt up above. He kept throwing dirt onto it until it reached the wall of the city, and it was still boiling. It reached Sayhabin, and the people were stirred up, and he wanted to send an army against them or to appoint a man over them.

Then Bukht Nasr came to him, spoke with him and said: "The one I sent that time was weak, and I have entered the city and heard the speech of its people. [So send me]." He sent him, and Bukht Nasr set out until, when they reached that place, [they fortified themselves] against him in their cities, and he could not overcome them. When the stay grew hard for them and his companions became hungry, they wished to return. An old woman from among the old women of the Children of Israel came out to him and said: "Where is the commander of the army?" He was brought to her, and she said to him: "It has reached me that you intend [.....] [[an illegible word.]] and then return with your army before you conquer this city." He said: "Yes, my stay has been long and my companions are hungry. I cannot remain beyond what has happened to me." She said: "Tell me, if I open the city for you, will you give me what I ask: that you kill whomever I order you to kill and refrain when I order you to refrain?" He said to her: "Yes." She said: "When morning comes, divide your army into four quarters, then station a quarter at each corner, then raise your hands to heaven and call out: 'We seek victory from You, O Allah, by the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariya,' for it will [collapse]." They did so, and the city collapsed, and they entered from its sides. She said to him: "Withhold your hand and turn to this blood until it calms." She took him to the blood of Yahya while it was on [much dust], and he killed upon it until it calmed. He killed seventy thousand. When the blood had calmed, she said to him: "Withhold your hand, for when Allah the Exalted kills a prophet, He is not satisfied until He kills those who killed him, and those who were pleased with his killing." The owner of the document came to him with a document, and he refrained from them and from the people of his household. He ruined Jerusalem and ordered that carrion be cast into it. He said: "Whoever casts carrion into it, he has his tax for that year." Allah aided him in the ruin of Rome, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya.

When Bukht Nasr ruined it, he took with him the notables and nobles of the Children of Israel. He took Daniel, Ali, Azariah and Mishael; all of these were from the descendants of the prophets. He also took with him the head of Jalut. When he arrived in the land of Babylon, he found that Sayhabin had died, so he became king in his place.
