The waw is omitted here both in pronunciation and in writing, but not in meaning, because it is in the nominative position. Its omission is due to the dropping of the following sukun letter, as in His words: ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [Surah al-Alaq: 18], ﴿Allah will erase falsehood﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 24], ﴿and Allah will give to the believers﴾, and ﴿and the caller will call﴾. ﴿But warnings do not avail﴾. The meaning of the verse: ﴿man prays﴾ against his wealth, his children and himself with evil, saying when he is distressed or angry, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, destroy him." ﴿His prayer for good﴾ means like his prayer to his Lord that He grant him well-being and blessing and preserve him in his self, wealth and children. ﴿For evil, it would destroy him,﴾ but Allah in His grace does not answer him in that. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [Surah Yunus: 11]. ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, hastening to supplicate against what he dislikes, which is answered for him in that.

Mujahid and a group of exegetes said, and Ibn Abbas said: ﴿man﴾ means one who is impatient, with no patience in ease or in hardship.

Some exegetes said: the ﴿man﴾ intended is Adam.

Salman al-Farisi said: The first thing Allah created of Adam was his head. He began to look while his body was being created. When it reached the time of 'Asr, his two legs were left without the spirit being breathed into them. He said, "O Lord, hasten [the creation] before nightfall." That is His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah created Adam's head, he looked at his body and was pleased with it. He went to stand up but could not. This is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾ It was also said: the intended one is Adam, for when the spirit reached his navel, he tried to stand up but fell. It is narrated that he was taken captive and came to Sawda bint Zam'a, who had mercy on him because of his groaning and loosened his bonds. He fled, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed against her that her hand be cut off. Then he regretted it and said: "O Allah, I am only a human being. Whomever I curse, make my supplication for him a mercy." Then this verse was revealed. [Note from the margin of the manuscript.]

﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, two indications and two signs of Our oneness, Our existence, the perfection of Our knowledge and Our power, and the counting of years and reckoning. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾.

Abu al-Tufayl said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), "What is this blackness in the moon?" Ali said: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾, and that is the effacement [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/64.].

Ibn Abbas said: Allah made the light of the sun seventy parts and the light of the moon seventy parts. Then He effaced from the light of the moon sixty-nine parts and added them to the light of the sun. So the sun has one hundred and thirty-nine parts, and the moon has one part [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/227.].

﴿And We made the sign of the day﴾, which is the sun, ﴿visible﴾ [bright and luminous]. [So it is in the original.]

Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: It means that it gives sight.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is from the saying of the Arabs, "The day became visible (absara al-nahar)" when it became bright and came to a state in which it could be seen.

Some said: It is like their saying, "a man is wicked and made wicked (khabith, mukhabbath) when his companions are wicked," and "a man is weakened (mudda'if) when his mounts are weak." Thus the day is "visible" when its people are seeing [A reconstruction from Tafsir al-Qurtubi; the manuscript is illegible.].

﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And We have explained it in detail﴾, meaning We have made it clear with explanation.

Muqatil ibn Ali narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah completed His creation, and nothing of His creation remained except Adam, He created a sun from the light of His Throne and a moon, and both were two suns. As for what was in Allah's foreknowledge that it would remain a sun, He created it like the world, between its eastern and western points. As for what was in His foreknowledge that He would obliterate and convert it into a moon, He created it inferior to the sun in greatness. But their smallness is only seen because of the great height of the sky and its distance from the earth. If Allah had left the sun and moon as He created them, no one would know night from day, nor day from night. The hired worker would not know until when he works and when he takes his wage. The fasting person would not know until when he fasts and when he breaks his fast. A woman would not know how to observe her waiting period. Muslims would not know the time of their prayers or the time of their pilgrimage. The debtor would not know when his debt falls due, and people would not know when to sow and plant for their livelihood, or when to rest their bodies. So the Lord, glory be to Him, was more considerate to His servants and more merciful to them. He sent Gabriel, who passed his wing over the face of the moon, which was then a sun, and wiped out its light, and its radiance remained in it. This is His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾. The meaning of the verse: ﴿man prays﴾ against his wealth, his children and himself with evil, saying when he is distressed or angry, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, destroy him." ﴿His prayer for good﴾ means like his prayer to his Lord that He grant him well-being and blessing and preserve him in his self, wealth and children. ﴿For evil, it would destroy him,﴾ but Allah in His grace does not answer him in that. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [Surah Yunus: 11]. ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, hastening to supplicate against what he dislikes, which is answered for him in that.

Mujahid and a group of exegetes said, and Ibn Abbas said: ﴿man﴾ means one who is impatient, with no patience in ease or in hardship.

Some exegetes said: the ﴿man﴾ intended is Adam.

Salman al-Farisi said: The first thing Allah created of Adam was his head. He began to look while his body was being created. When it reached the time of 'Asr, his two legs were left without the spirit being breathed into them. He said, "O Lord, hasten [the creation] before nightfall." That is His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah created Adam's head, he looked at his body and was pleased with it. He went to stand up but could not. This is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾ It was also said: the intended one is Adam, for when the spirit reached his navel, he tried to stand up but fell. It is narrated that he was taken captive and came to Sawda bint Zam'a, who had mercy on him because of his groaning and loosened his bonds. He fled, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed against her that her hand be cut off. Then he regretted it and said: "O Allah, I am only a human being. Whomever I curse, make my supplication for him a mercy." Then this verse was revealed. [Note from the margin of the manuscript.]

﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, two indications and two signs of Our oneness, Our existence, the perfection of Our knowledge and Our power, and the counting of years and reckoning. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾.

Abu al-Tufayl said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), "What is this blackness in the moon?" Ali said: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾, and that is the effacement [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/64.].

Ibn Abbas said: Allah made the light of the sun seventy parts and the light of the moon seventy parts. Then He effaced from the light of the moon sixty-nine parts and added them to the light of the sun. So the sun has one hundred and thirty-nine parts, and the moon has one part [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/227.].

﴿And We made the sign of the day﴾, which is the sun, ﴿visible﴾ [bright and luminous]. [So it is in the original.]

Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: It means that it gives sight.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is from the saying of the Arabs, "The day became visible (absara al-nahar)" when it became bright and came to a state in which it could be seen.

Some said: It is like their saying, "a man is wicked and made wicked (khabith, mukhabbath) when his companions are wicked," and "a man is weakened (mudda'if) when his mounts are weak." Thus the day is "visible" when its people are seeing [A reconstruction from Tafsir al-Qurtubi; the manuscript is illegible.].

﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And We have explained it in detail﴾, meaning We have made it clear with explanation.

Muqatil ibn Ali narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah completed His creation, and nothing of His creation remained except Adam, He created a sun from the light of His Throne and a moon, and both were two suns. As for what was in Allah's foreknowledge that it would remain a sun, He created it like the world, between its eastern and western points. As for what was in His foreknowledge that He would obliterate and convert it into a moon, He created it inferior to the sun in greatness. But their smallness is only seen because of the great height of the sky and its distance from the earth. If Allah had left the sun and moon as He created them, no one would know night from day, nor day from night. The hired worker would not know until when he works and when he takes his wage. The fasting person would not know until when he fasts and when he breaks his fast. A woman would not know how to observe her waiting period. Muslims would not know the time of their prayers or the time of their pilgrimage. The debtor would not know when his debt falls due, and people would not know when to sow and plant for their livelihood, or when to rest their bodies. So the Lord, glory be to Him, was more considerate to His servants and more merciful to them. He sent Gabriel, who passed his wing over the face of the moon, which was then a sun, and wiped out its light, and its radiance remained in it. This is His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾. The meaning of the verse: ﴿man prays﴾ against his wealth, his children and himself with evil, saying when he is distressed or angry, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, destroy him." ﴿His prayer for good﴾ means like his prayer to his Lord that He grant him well-being and blessing and preserve him in his self, wealth and children. ﴿For evil, it would destroy him,﴾ but Allah in His grace does not answer him in that. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [Surah Yunus: 11]. ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, hastening to supplicate against what he dislikes, which is answered for him in that.

Mujahid and a group of exegetes said, and Ibn Abbas said: ﴿man﴾ means one who is impatient, with no patience in ease or in hardship.

Some exegetes said: the ﴿man﴾ intended is Adam.

Salman al-Farisi said: The first thing Allah created of Adam was his head. He began to look while his body was being created. When it reached the time of 'Asr, his two legs were left without the spirit being breathed into them. He said, "O Lord, hasten [the creation] before nightfall." That is His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah created Adam's head, he looked at his body and was pleased with it. He went to stand up but could not. This is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾ It was also said: the intended one is Adam, for when the spirit reached his navel, he tried to stand up but fell. It is narrated that he was taken captive and came to Sawda bint Zam'a, who had mercy on him because of his groaning and loosened his bonds. He fled, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed against her that her hand be cut off. Then he regretted it and said: "O Allah, I am only a human being. Whomever I curse, make my supplication for him a mercy." Then this verse was revealed. [Note from the margin of the manuscript.]

﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, two indications and two signs of Our oneness, Our existence, the perfection of Our knowledge and Our power, and the counting of years and reckoning. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾.

Abu al-Tufayl said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), "What is this blackness in the moon?" Ali said: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾, and that is the effacement [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/64.].

Ibn Abbas said: Allah made the light of the sun seventy parts and the light of the moon seventy parts. Then He effaced from the light of the moon sixty-nine parts and added them to the light of the sun. So the sun has one hundred and thirty-nine parts, and the moon has one part [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/227.].

﴿And We made the sign of the day﴾, which is the sun, ﴿visible﴾ [bright and luminous]. [So it is in the original.]

Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: It means that it gives sight.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is from the saying of the Arabs, "The day became visible (absara al-nahar)" when it became bright and came to a state in which it could be seen.

Some said: It is like their saying, "a man is wicked and made wicked (khabith, mukhabbath) when his companions are wicked," and "a man is weakened (mudda'if) when his mounts are weak." Thus the day is "visible" when its people are seeing [A reconstruction from Tafsir al-Qurtubi; the manuscript is illegible.].

﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And We have explained it in detail﴾, meaning We have made it clear with explanation.

Muqatil ibn Ali narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah completed His creation, and nothing of His creation remained except Adam, He created a sun from the light of His Throne and a moon, and both were two suns. As for what was in Allah's foreknowledge that it would remain a sun, He created it like the world, between its eastern and western points. As for what was in His foreknowledge that He would obliterate and convert it into a moon, He created it inferior to the sun in greatness. But their smallness is only seen because of the great height of the sky and its distance from the earth. If Allah had left the sun and moon as He created them, no one would know night from day, nor day from night. The hired worker would not know until when he works and when he takes his wage. The fasting person would not know until when he fasts and when he breaks his fast. A woman would not know how to observe her waiting period. Muslims would not know the time of their prayers or the time of their pilgrimage. The debtor would not know when his debt falls due, and people would not know when to sow and plant for their livelihood, or when to rest their bodies. So the Lord, glory be to Him, was more considerate to His servants and more merciful to them. He sent Gabriel, who passed his wing over the face of the moon, which was then a sun, and wiped out its light, and its radiance remained in it. This is His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: His good and evil are with him; they do not leave him until he is held accountable for them. [Al-Hasan recited: ﴿on the right and on the left, seated﴾.] Then he said: "O son of Adam, your record has been spread out, and two angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your [left. As for the one on your right, he records your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he records your bad deeds. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: By "omen" is meant what was decreed for him, that He would make him act in such a way as to lead to his destiny of happiness or wretchedness. Yahya ibn Wathhab read: ﴿wayukhriju﴾, meaning: and Allah brings it forth.

It may also mean what is indicated by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best wealth is a foaled mare or a palm row in pollen," [Al-Sikkah: a row of palm trees arranged in a line; al-ma'burah: pollinated. The meaning: the best wealth is offspring and crops.] [21] [Al-Ahad wa al-Mathani of al-Dahhak: 2/424; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 7/91.] He meant by "ma'murah" a multiplication of offspring, and it is said of a large amount: "amr," and its verb is "amara": "they increased in number (amaru)" when they multiplied.

Labid said:

"All the sons of the free-born, their end is small, even if they multiply in number.
If they are envied, they will be humbled, and if they increase, one day they will come to destruction and ruin."

This was preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, and it is the reading of the majority.

Abu Ubayd said: We chose this reading because the three meanings come together in it, namely command, sign (amara), and multiplication.

﴿Its affluent ones﴾ [...] [An illegible word; perhaps: "creation."] They are its wealthy and its leaders. ﴿Then they transgressed therein, and the word became due against it﴾, meaning: the punishment became obligatory for it. ﴿So We destroyed it with complete destruction﴾.

That is: We recompensed them [and destroyed them with a destruction through a matter wondrous in its nature].

Ma'mar narrated from al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered one day upon [Zaynab], saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a breach has been opened in the wall of Gog and Magog, like this," [and he made a circle with his thumb and forefinger]. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/73.] [22]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 17, verses 9–16:**

﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright,﴾ meaning the path that is most straight, most just and most correct [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/225.]]. ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that for them is a great reward,﴾ which is Paradise, ﴿and that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment,﴾ which is the Fire. ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good﴾. The waw is omitted here both in pronunciation and in writing, but not in meaning, because it is in the nominative position. Its omission is due to the dropping of the following sukun letter, as in His words: ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [Surah al-Alaq: 18], ﴿Allah will erase falsehood﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 24], ﴿and Allah will give to the believers﴾, and ﴿and the caller will call﴾. ﴿But warnings do not avail﴾. The meaning of the verse: ﴿man prays﴾ against his wealth, his children and himself with evil, saying when he is distressed or angry, "O Allah, curse him, O Allah, destroy him." ﴿His prayer for good﴾ means like his prayer to his Lord that He grant him well-being and blessing and preserve him in his self, wealth and children. ﴿For evil, it would destroy him,﴾ but Allah in His grace does not answer him in that. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect meeting Us in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [Surah Yunus: 11]. ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, hastening to supplicate against what he dislikes, which is answered for him in that.

Mujahid and a group of exegetes said, and Ibn Abbas said: ﴿man﴾ means one who is impatient, with no patience in ease or in hardship.

Some exegetes said: the ﴿man﴾ intended is Adam.

Salman al-Farisi said: The first thing Allah created of Adam was his head. He began to look while his body was being created. When it reached the time of 'Asr, his two legs were left without the spirit being breathed into them. He said, "O Lord, hasten [the creation] before nightfall." That is His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah created Adam's head, he looked at his body and was pleased with it. He went to stand up but could not. This is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty.﴾ It was also said: the intended one is Adam, for when the spirit reached his navel, he tried to stand up but fell. It is narrated that he was taken captive and came to Sawda bint Zam'a, who had mercy on him because of his groaning and loosened his bonds. He fled, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed against her that her hand be cut off. Then he regretted it and said: "O Allah, I am only a human being. Whomever I curse, make my supplication for him a mercy." Then this verse was revealed. [Note from the margin of the manuscript.]

﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, two indications and two signs of Our oneness, Our existence, the perfection of Our knowledge and Our power, and the counting of years and reckoning. ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night﴾.

Abu al-Tufayl said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), "What is this blackness in the moon?" Ali said: ﴿Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾, and that is the effacement [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/64.].

Ibn Abbas said: Allah made the light of the sun seventy parts and the light of the moon seventy parts. Then He effaced from the light of the moon sixty-nine parts and added them to the light of the sun. So the sun has one hundred and thirty-nine parts, and the moon has one part [see Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/227.].

﴿And We made the sign of the day﴾, which is the sun, ﴿visible﴾ [bright and luminous]. [So it is in the original.]

Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said: It means that it gives sight.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is from the saying of the Arabs, "The day became visible (absara al-nahar)" when it became bright and came to a state in which it could be seen.

Some said: It is like their saying, "a man is wicked and made wicked (khabith, mukhabbath) when his companions are wicked," and "a man is weakened (mudda'if) when his mounts are weak." Thus the day is "visible" when its people are seeing [A reconstruction from Tafsir al-Qurtubi; the manuscript is illegible.].

﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And We have explained it in detail﴾, meaning We have made it clear with explanation.

Muqatil ibn Ali narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah completed His creation, and nothing of His creation remained except Adam, He created a sun from the light of His Throne and a moon, and both were two suns. As for what was in Allah's foreknowledge that it would remain a sun, He created it like the world, between its eastern and western points. As for what was in His foreknowledge that He would obliterate and convert it into a moon, He created it inferior to the sun in greatness. But their smallness is only seen because of the great height of the sky and its distance from the earth. If Allah had left the sun and moon as He created them, no one would know night from day, nor day from night. The hired worker would not know until when he works and when he takes his wage. The fasting person would not know until when he fasts and when he breaks his fast. A woman would not know how to observe her waiting period. Muslims would not know the time of their prayers or the time of their pilgrimage. The debtor would not know when his debt falls due, and people would not know when to sow and plant for their livelihood, or when to rest their bodies. So the Lord, glory be to Him, was more considerate to His servants and more merciful to them. He sent Gabriel, who passed his wing over the face of the moon, which was then a sun, and wiped out its light, and its radiance remained in it. This is His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible﴾. The [darkness] [So in the original.] that you see in the middle of the moon, resembling lines, is the trace of the effacement." [Mentioned briefly by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-Mawdu'at: 1/139.]

﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾. Ibn Abbas said: Whatever he is destined [of good and evil] is his constant companion wherever he is [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/229.].

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: His good and evil are with him; they do not leave him until he is held accountable for them. [Al-Hasan recited: ﴿on the right and on the left, seated﴾.] Then he said: "O son of Adam, your record has been spread out, and two angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your [left. As for the one on your right, he records your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he records your bad deeds. So do what you wish, little or much, until when you die, your record is rolled up and placed on your neck, with you in your grave, until you come out on the Day of Resurrection,] ﴿a book he will find laid open﴾ [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/69.].

Mujahid: his deeds and his provision. He also narrated: No child is born except that on his neck is a written paper saying whether he is wretched or happy.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: By "omen" is meant what was decreed for him, that He would make him act in such a way as to lead to his destiny of happiness or wretchedness. It was expressed as "omen" according to the custom of the Arabs, who would take omens from the flights of birds, from what passes to the right or left [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/66.].

Abu Ubayd and al-'Ayni said: By "omen" is meant his share of good and evil, from their saying, "So-and-so's omen went out with such-and-such," meaning that his omen ran with such-and-such for him.

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Abu Raja' read: ﴿ta'irahu﴾ in his neck, without an alif. The neck was specified over his other limbs because the neck is the place of marks, of necklaces, and of things that either disgrace or adorn. The speech of the Arabs thus ascribes things that are attached to the necks, so they say, "This is on my neck until I come out of it," and "This thing is attached to his neck."

﴿And We bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book﴾. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin and Ya'qub read: ﴿wayakhruju﴾ with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the ra, meaning: the omen goes forth for him on the Day of Resurrection as a book, the word ﴿kitaban﴾ being in the accusative as a state (hal). It may also mean that the omen goes forth and becomes a book.

Abu Ja'far read: ﴿wayukhraju﴾ with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the ra, in the passive form, meaning: the omen is brought forth for him as a book.

Yahya ibn Wathhab read: ﴿wayukhriju﴾, meaning: and Allah brings it forth.

The rest read: with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the ra, meaning: ﴿and We bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book﴾, with ﴿kitaban﴾ in the accusative as the object of the bringing forth. Abu Amr argued for this reading by His saying: ﴿We have fastened it﴾.

﴿Yalqahu﴾: Abu Amir and Abu Ja'far read: ﴿tulaqqahu﴾ with a damma on the ta and a shadda on the qaf, meaning: the person encounters that book, that is, it is brought to him. The rest read with a fatha on the ya, meaning: he sees it.

﴿Manshuran﴾ is in the accusative as a state.

From Bistam ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu al-Nabbaj say: I heard Abu al-Sawwar al-Adawi recite this verse, then he said: "Two spreadings. And upon you, as long as you live, O son of Adam, your record is spread out, so do in it whatever you wish. When you die, it is rolled up, and when you are resurrected, it is spread out again."

﴿Read your book; sufficient is yourself today as a reckoner against you﴾, meaning: it will be said to him, "Read your book," [and] a reckoner, one who recompenses.

Qatadah: On that day everyone who was not in this world will read [recompensing] [So in the original.].

Al-Hasan said: [Allah has indeed been just to you] by making you the reckoner of yourself.

﴿Whoever is guided, he is only guided for his own self, and whoever goes astray, he only goes astray to its detriment﴾, because upon it is its punishment. ﴿No bearer bears the burden of another﴾, and no one carrying a load bears another's sin. ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾, establishing proof against them through the signs that cut off their excuse. ﴿And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones﴾.

ʿUthman al-Nahdi, Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi, Abu al-ʿAliyah, [Abu Ja'far] and Mujahid read: ﴿amarna﴾ with a shadda on the mim, meaning: We mixed its wicked ones [So in the original.], so they disobeyed therein, and when they did that, We destroyed them.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Hayah al-Shami and Ya'qub read: ﴿amarna﴾ with a long vowel, meaning: We increased them.

The rest read with a kasra on the mim, meaning: We commanded them to obedience, and they disobeyed. It may also mean: We made them a command (amr), because the Arabs say, "amr ghayr ma'mur," meaning: not commanded. It may also mean what is indicated by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best wealth is a foaled mare or a palm row in pollen," [Al-Sikkah: a row of palm trees arranged in a line; al-ma'burah: pollinated. The meaning: the best wealth is offspring and crops.] [21] [Al-Ahad wa al-Mathani of al-Dahhak: 2/424; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 7/91.] He meant by "ma'murah" a multiplication of offspring, and it is said of a large amount: "amr," and its verb is "amara": "they increased in number (amaru)" when they multiplied.

Labid said:

"All the sons of the free-born, their end is small, even if they multiply in number.
If they are envied, they will be humbled, and if they increase, one day they will come to destruction and ruin."

This was preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, and it is the reading of the majority.

Abu Ubayd said: We chose this reading because the three meanings come together in it, namely command, sign (amara), and multiplication.

﴿Its affluent ones﴾ [...] [An illegible word; perhaps: "creation."] They are its wealthy and its leaders. ﴿Then they transgressed therein, and the word became due against it﴾, meaning: the punishment became obligatory for it. ﴿So We destroyed it with complete destruction﴾.

That is: We recompensed them [and destroyed them with a destruction through a matter wondrous in its nature].

Ma'mar narrated from al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered one day upon [Zaynab], saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a breach has been opened in the wall of Gog and Magog, like this," [and he made a circle with his thumb and forefinger]. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/73.] [22]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verses 17–25:

﴿How many generations have We destroyed after Noah?﴾ This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And your Lord is sufficient as one who is Knowing and Seeing of the sins of His servants.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the length of a generation (qarn):

ʿAbdullah ibn Abi (Ibn Abi Dawud) said: A qarn is one hundred and twenty years. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent at the beginning of the first qarn, and the last of them was Yazid ibn Muʿawiya.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn Bashir al-Mazini that the Prophet (ﷺ) placed his hand on his head and said: "This boy will live a qarn." I asked: "What is the qarn?" He said: "One hundred years."

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim said: "We kept counting for him until he completed one hundred years, and then he died."

al-Kalbi said: A qarn is eighty years.

ʿUmar ibn Shakir narrated from Ibn Sirin, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A qarn is forty years." [23]

﴿Whoever desires the immediate [life]﴾, meaning this world. Here a particle is used in place of a noun, and by "the immediate abode" he meant this world. ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We desire﴾, with expansion and restriction, for whom We wish to be treated thus, [at first] by destruction. ﴿Then We have made for him Hell; he will burn in it, censured and expelled﴾, driven away and distanced. ﴿But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due effort, while he is a believer — those are whose effort is appreciated﴾, accepted, not rejected. ﴿To each — these and those — We extend﴾, meaning We extend to each of the two groups, those who desire the immediate life and those who desire the Hereafter, so that We provide both of them altogether ﴿from the gift of your Lord﴾, then their circumstances differ in wealth. ﴿And the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾, prevented or withheld from His servants. ﴿Look, O Muhammad, how We have favoured some of them over others﴾ in provision and in deeds, meaning the seeker of the immediate life and the seeker of the Hereafter. ﴿And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favour.﴾ ﴿Do not make with Allah another god, lest you sit [in disgrace], censured and forsaken.﴾ The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is others. ﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah and al-Hasan said. Zakariyya ibn Salam said: A man came to al-Hasan and said that he had divorced his wife three times. He said: "You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has become irrevocably separated from you." The man said: "This is what Allah decreed for me."

al-Hasan, who was eloquent, said: "What Allah decreed" means what Allah commanded. He then recited this verse: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾. The people said: "al-Hasan has spoken about qadar (divine predestination)." [The phrase is "qadar" in the text.]

Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: "And your Lord has enjoined," and the evidence for this interpretation is the recitation of ʿAli, ʿAbdullah and Ubayy: ﴿And your Lord has enjoined﴾ (wa-wassa rabbuka).

Abu Ishaq al-Kufi narrated from Shurayk ibn Mazahim that he recited (wa-wassa) and said: "They assimilated the waw into the sad, so it became a qaf." [In the text: "wa-qada" with the letter changed.]

al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: "[And your Lord has commanded] that you worship none but Him, and kindness to the two parents," meaning: He commanded kindness to both parents, being dutiful to them and tender towards them. [[Thus in the original.]]

﴿If one of them or both reach old age with you﴾. al-Kisaʾi read it with an alif (yablughanna, with alif in the verb form "yablughan ... aḥaduhuma"), while the rest read yablughanna without alif, referring to the singular. According to this reading, the phrase ﴿one of them or both﴾ is a new (independent) sentence, like the verse ﴿They became blind and deaf, many of them﴾ and the verse ﴿and they secretly conferred﴾. Then he begins: ﴿Do not say to them, "Uff."﴾ In this word there are three dialectal forms with a fatha on the fa, which is the reading of the people of Makkah and Syria and the choice of Yaʿqub and Suhayl. "Uff" with kasra and tanwin is the reading of the people of Madinah, Ayyub and Hafs. "Uffi" with kasra and no tanwin is the reading of the other reciters. All these are well-known dialects with one meaning.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is a word of aversion. Muqatil said: It is harsh and rough speech.

Abu ʿUbayd said: The origin of uff and tuff is the dirt on the fingers when you rub it. Others distinguished between them: uff is the sweat and dirt that accumulates in the armpits, and tuff is what accumulates between the fingers. It is also said: uff is earwax and tuff is the dirt under the nails. It is also said: uff is the dirt of the fingernail, and tuff is whatever you lift from the ground with your hand of something insignificant.

﴿And do not repel them﴾, do not scold them. ﴿And speak to them a noble word﴾, good and gracious.

Ibn al-Musayyab said: Like the speech of a sinful slave to a harsh master. [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/84.]

ʿAtaʾ said: Do not name them or address them by their kunya; say to them: "O my father" and "O my mother."

Mujahid on this verse said: If they reach the age when they urinate and defecate, then do not disgust them.

Do not say to them "Uff" when you see harm from them, and remove from them their excrement and urine, just as they removed these from you when you were a child. [And do not harm them.] [[Thus in the original.]] [Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated that the disobedient child dies a bad death.

A man said to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family): "My parents have reached such old age that I attend to them as they attended to me in childhood. Have I repaid them?" He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: "No. For they used to do this for you while they loved your survival, and you do it while you wish for their death."] [[From the margin of the manuscript.]] [24]

﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy.﴾

ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr said: "Their right is such that he should not refuse them anything that he can give life to."

Muqatil said: "Be gentle to them, lower your side to them, and be humble before them."

al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read: janāḥa al-dhill with a kasra on the dhal, meaning: do not be difficult with them.

﴿And say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small."﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas said: This is abrogated (naskh, meaning the ruling has been replaced) by the verse: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were of near kin﴾, and so on.

Shuʿbah narrated from Yaʿla ibn ʿAtaʾ from his father from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"The pleasure of Allah the Exalted is with the pleasure of the parents, and the anger of Allah is with the anger of the parents." [25] [[Subul al-Salam of al-ʿAsqalani: 4/164, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/172.]]

ʿAtaʾ narrated from ʿAʾishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is said to the disobedient child: Do whatever you wish, for I will not forgive you. And it is said to the dutiful child: Do whatever you wish, for I forgive you." [26] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 16/476.]]

ʿAtaʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends the evening and the morning pleasing his parents, for him there are two doors open to Paradise. And whoever spends the evening and the morning angering his parents, for him there are two doors to the Fire, and if only one [of them is angry], then one [door]." [27] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/245.]]

A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if they wronged him?" He said: "Even if they wronged him," three times.

Rashid ibn Saʿd narrated from Abu Hani al-Khawlani from Abu ʿUmar al-Qasabi [[Thus in the original.]], who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, guide me to a deed by which I may draw near to Allah." He said: "Do you have a mother and a father?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then with dutifulness to the parents, the small deed suffices." [28]

﴿Your Lord is most knowing of what is in your souls﴾ concerning dutifulness to parents and disobedience to them. ﴿If you are righteous﴾, dutiful and obedient in what Allah has commanded you, after a shortcoming on your part in fulfilling the rights of your parents that were obligatory upon you, and other obligations of Allah. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving to those who return (awwabin)﴾, after disobedience and error.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said regarding this verse: It is the man who hastens to his parents, desiring nothing but good, for he will not be held accountable for it.

The exegetes differed on the meaning of al-awwabin:

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: Those who return to good. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: The one who sins, then repents, then sins, then repents.

Mujahid from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar: It is the one who remembers his sins in private and then seeks forgiveness from Allah for them.

ʿAmr ibn Dinar: It is the one who says: "O Allah, forgive me for what I committed in this gathering of mine."

Ibn ʿAbbas: The one who returns to Allah regarding what has befallen him and what he intends. The word awwab is on the pattern fazzal (intensive form) from awba, meaning he returned.

ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras said: "Every absent one returns, but the one absent by death does not return."

ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil said, and it is the narration of Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbas: The evidence is His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him﴾. [Al-Sabaʾ: 10.]

al-Walibi said: They are the obedient and humble.

Qatadah: The ones who pray. ʿAwn al-ʿUqayli: They are those who pray the forenoon prayer (ṣalat al-ḍuḥa).

Ibn al-Munkadir: Between maghrib and ʿisha.

Ibn Idris narrated from his father from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: "The awwabin are the eager ones (al-raghibin)."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verses 17–25:

﴿How many generations have We destroyed after Noah?﴾ This is a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And your Lord is sufficient as one who is Knowing and Seeing of the sins of His servants.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the length of a generation (qarn):

ʿAbdullah ibn Abi (Ibn Abi Dawud) said: A qarn is one hundred and twenty years. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent at the beginning of the first qarn, and the last of them was Yazid ibn Muʿawiya.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn Bashir al-Mazini that the Prophet (ﷺ) placed his hand on his head and said: "This boy will live a qarn." I asked: "What is the qarn?" He said: "One hundred years."

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim said: "We kept counting for him until he completed one hundred years, and then he died."

al-Kalbi said: A qarn is eighty years.
