The swimmer comes to the one who has gathered the stones before him, and he opens his mouth, and he puts a stone in it; then he goes off swimming, and then returns to him, and he opens his mouth [sic, as in the original] and he puts a stone in it. I said: "What is this?" They said: "Come along." So I went and came to a man of the most hideous appearance, the ugliest man I have ever seen, and beside him was a fire, which he was stoking and running around it. I said to them: "What is this?" They said: "Come along." So we went and came to a verdant garden [thick with growth], containing every kind of spring flower, and there was a great tree, and at its root an elderly tall man, and around him children, more than I have ever seen. I said: "Who are these?" They said: "Come along." So we went and came to a great tree, larger than any tree I have ever seen, and [no more beautiful]. They said to me: "Ascend," so we ascended and reached a city built of gold and silver bricks. We came to the gate of the city and asked for it to be opened, and it was opened for us, and we entered. There we were met by men, half of whose creation was [as beautiful as] the most beautiful I have seen, and half [as ugly as] the ugliest I have seen. They said to them: "Go and plunge into that river," and there was a river flowing across, as if it were churned milk for its whiteness. They went and plunged into it, then returned to us, and the evil had left them, and they became in the best form. He said: I said to them, "By God, I have never seen anything as wondrous as tonight; what is this that I have seen?" They said: "We will inform you. As for the one whose head you saw being smashed with the rock, he is a man who takes the Qur'an and rejects it and sleeps through the obligatory prayer. As for the one whose cheek, eye and nostril you saw being torn to his nape, he is a man [who goes out] from his house and tells a lie that reaches the horizons [the lie spreads to every region]." [[supplied from al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

As for the naked men and women in the oven-like building, they are the fornicators, male and female. As for the man swimming in the river and swallowing stones, he is the consumer of usury. As for the hideous man beside the fire that he stokes, he is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. As for the tall man in the [garden], he is Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and as for the children around him, every child is born upon the fitrah.

As for the people who were half beautiful and half ugly, they are people who "mixed a righteous deed with another evil," so Allah pardoned them. As for the garden, it is "Gardens of Eden," and as for the city I entered, it is the abode of the martyrs.

He said: "While my gaze was rising, there was something like a white fly." They said to me: "This is your abode." I am Jibril, and this is Mika'il. I said: "May Allah bless you both; let me enter my abode." They said: "There remains for you something you have not completed; had you completed it, you would have entered your abode." [37] [[in full in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur 3/274, with slight variation.]]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is the vision in which he saw that he and his companions would enter Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, while he was in Madinah at that time. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hastened toward Makkah before the appointed time, but the polytheists turned him back.

Some people said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it." So his return became a trial for them. Then in the following year the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for it and entered it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Hudhayfah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, on the saying of Allah, ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾, said: He saw the Banu Umayyah on the pulpits, and that distressed him. It was said to him: "It is only the world, which they are given, [and it is withheld] from him." ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾: a test for the people.

Abd al-Muhaymin narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the Banu Umayyah leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that distressed him, so he was never seen laughing until he died. Thereupon Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the cursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an﴾, meaning the tree of Zaqqum.

The meaning of the verse: "the cursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an" is connected by "al-shajarah" being conjoined to "al-ru'ya." Its interpretation: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you, and the cursed tree in the Qur'an, except as a trial for the people." So their trial in the vision was what has been mentioned, and their trial in the cursed tree was that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Is it not a lie that Ibn Abi Kabshah threatens you with burning by stones, then claims that a tree will grow in it, though you know that fire burns trees? So what do they say about the Zaqqum?"

'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari [sic, as in the original] said: "It is butter and dates in the Berber language."

Abu Jahl said: "O slave girl, bring us zaqqum." She brought him butter and dates. He said: "O people, this is what Muhammad frightens you with; by God, Zaqqum is only known as butter and dates." Then Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾ [[Surah al-Dukhan: 43, 44.]] and described it in al-Saffat: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire﴾ [[Surah al-Saffat: 64.]], meaning that it was created from fire and fashioned from it. And Allah revealed: ﴿And We warn them, but it increases them only in great transgression﴾.

Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from a client of the Banu Hashim who told him that 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal [sent] [[as in the original.]] to Ibn 'Abbas: "Are we the cursed tree in the Qur'an?" He said: He said: "The cursed tree is this tree that twines around trees," meaning the dodder (kushuth). [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/286.]]

﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He said: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ meaning from clay.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Lord of Might sent Iblis, and he took a handful of the surface of the earth, of its sweet and salty parts, and from it created Adam. So everything He created from its sweet part is destined for happiness even if it is the son of two disbelievers, and everything He created from its salty part is destined for wretchedness even if it is the son of two prophets.

He said: For this reason Iblis said: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?" meaning: "This clay—I brought it." For this reason Adam was named, because he was created from the surface of the earth. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/145.]]

He said: ﴿Iblis said: "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants,"﴾ i.e., I will surely take control of his offspring, gather them, and destroy them through misguidance, and utterly uproot them. It is said: "Fulan ihtanaka what Fulan has of knowledge or perfection," meaning he took it all, extracted and seized it entirely. And "the locust ihtanaka the crop" when it eats it all. The poet said:

"I complain to You of a year that has ravaged,
and has stripped our wealth and uprooted it."

It is also said that it is from the Arab saying: "hanaka al-dabbah yahnikuha" when one ties a rope under its lower jaw by which to lead it until it becomes steady.

﴿Except a few﴾, meaning the protected ones whom Allah excepted in His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 42.]]. He said: ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾, i.e., your recompense and the recompense of your followers, a complete reward. ﴿And incite﴾ [i.e., seize], ﴿entice, lead astray, and make them slide﴾ ﴿whomever you can among them﴾, i.e., among the offspring of Adam, ﴿with your voice﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "by your calling them to disobedience of Allah; every caller to disobedience is among the soldiers of Iblis."

Mujahid said: "by singing and musical instruments."

﴿And urge against them﴾, i.e., gather and shout. Muqatil: "entice them away from Him."

﴿with your horsemen and your footmen﴾, i.e., the riders of his army and his infantry.

The exegetes said: every rider and walker in disobedience to Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah: He has horsemen and footmen among the jinn and humans; whoever rides and fights in disobedience is from Iblis's horsemen, and whoever walks and fights in disobedience to Allah is from Iblis's footmen. "Rajil" means infantry.

Hafs recited "wa-rajilika" with a kasrah on the ra', and both are dialects: "rajil" and "rajil," like "tajir" and "tajir," and "rakib" and "rakib."

﴿And share with them in wealth﴾. Some people said: it is every wealth acquired unlawfully and spent unlawfully. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: it is usury. Qatadah: what the polytheists used to forbid of livestock, such as the bahair, the sawaib, the wasilah, and the hawami; this is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Dahhak said: it is what they used to slaughter for their gods.

﴿And the children.﴾

Some said: they are children of fornication. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Walibi from him: it is what they accepted from their children and committed unlawful acts with regard to them.

al-Hasan and Qatadah: the enemy of Allah shared with them in their wealth and children, so they were made Magians, Jews, and Christians, and dyed with other than the dye of Islam. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/152.]]

Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: his sharing with them in the children is in naming them their children: 'Abd al-Harith, 'Abd Shams, and 'Abd Fulan.

﴿And promise them﴾, and give them false hopes of obedience to you. Allah says: ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾, i.e., falsehood and deception, because he cannot avail them against the punishment of Allah when it descends upon them, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 22.]].

﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them; and sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs.﴾ ﴿Your Lord is He who drives [ships] for you [smoothly and makes them run]﴾ ﴿in the sea, to the saying: "and when harm touches you at sea"﴾, i.e., hardship befalls you [at sea], and you fear drowning, ﴿those you invoke vanish except Him﴾, i.e., except your supplication to Him, and you find nothing that suffices you other than Him. ﴿But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away﴾ from faith and obedience and disbelieve in what has come to you. ﴿And man has always been ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you at the side of the land, or send against you a sandstorm﴾, i.e., He will make you disappear and perish; or send against you a hasib: stones raining down upon you from the sky, as He rained upon the people of Lot.

Abu 'Ubayd and al-Qutaybi said: the hasib is that which pelts with pebbles, which are small stones.

al-Farazdaq said:
"Facing the north of Syria, it strikes us
with a hasib like scattered cotton fluff."

﴿Then you will not find for yourselves any protector. Or do you feel secure that He will return you into it [the sea] another time, and send against you a violent wind and drown you for your disbelief? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger.﴾ Qatadah: "qasifan" means a violent wind; Ibn 'Abbas and Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is that which shatters everything, i.e., crushes and breaks it, and it is what breaks trees.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "nakhsifa, nursila, nu'idukum, and nughriqakum" all with nun, because of His saying "'alayna" (against Us). The rest recited them all with ya', because of His saying "iyyah" (Him). Except Abu Ja'far, who recited "tughriqakum" with ta', meaning the wind.

﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam.﴾ Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam," said: every creature eats with its mouth except the son of Adam, who eats with his hands; and also from him: with intellect.

al-Dahhak: with speech and discernment.

'Ata': the balance and proportion of the general form and its extension. Yaman: with beauty of form.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: in that He made Muhammad among them. It is also said: men with beards and women with forelocks.

Muhammad ibn Jarir: in His giving them power over other creatures and subjecting all creatures to them.

﴿And We carried them on land and sea and provided for them of the good things﴾, meaning delicious foods and drinks.

Muqatil: ghee, butter, dates, and sweets, and the provision of others is what is hidden from you.

﴿And We preferred them over much of what We have created, with [marked] preference.﴾

Some people said: His saying "much of what We have created" is an exception for the angels.

al-Kalbi said: they are preferred over all creatures except a group of angels: Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and their like.

Others said: what is meant is all of what We have created; the Arabs sometimes place "the greater" and "the many" in the position of the plural and the whole, as in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar. They listen eagerly, and most of them are liars﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara: 222–223]], and what is meant is all the devils.

Ma'mar from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam," said: the angels said: "Our Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world to eat and enjoy in it, and You did not give us that; so give us the Hereafter." He said: "By My might and My majesty, I will not make the offspring of those whom I created with My hand like what I said to them: 'Be,' and it is."

Hammad ibn Salamah from Abu al-Mahram, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: "The believer is more honored by Allah than the angels who are with Him."

﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: with their prophet. What supports this is what al-Suddi narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying, "The Day We will call every people with their leader": he said, with their prophet.

Abu Salih, Abu Nadr, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: with their book which was revealed to them, and it is

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 60–72 (part 2 of 2):

The narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, and from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Murtada (peace be upon them), from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning "the Day We shall call every people with their imam": "Every people will be brought with the imam of their time, the Book of their Lord, and the Sunnah of their Prophet" [38].

Abu al-Aliyah and al-Hasan said: "with their deeds." The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, in the context of the verse, ﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record﴾, and its parallel, His saying ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register (imam mubin)﴾. Thus the Book is called an imam.

Ibn Shihab narrated from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever spends a pair [of things] in the cause of Allah will be called from the Gardens: 'O servant of Allah, this is good.' Whoever was among the people of prayer will be called from the Gate of Prayer; whoever was among the people of jihad will be called from the Gate of Jihad; whoever was among the people of charity will be called from the Gate of Charity; and whoever was among the people of fasting will be called from the Gate of al-Rayyan."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, there is no necessity for one called from those gates; but will anyone be called from all of them?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them" [39] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/227, and Sahih Muslim: 3/91.]].

The hadith of the banners and standards also confirms this statement.

Badhan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas: "with their imam" means the one who called them in this world to misguidance or to guidance.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah: "with their leaders in good and evil."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them imams calling to the Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 41.]], and it was said: "with their worshipped ones."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "with their mothers."

The wise have said: in this there are three aspects of wisdom. The first: for the sake of Isa (peace be upon him). The second: to honour the noble lineage of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). The third: so that the children of fornication are not exposed.

Regarding ﴿Whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾ up to His saying ﴿and whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind [in the Hereafter]﴾, the scholars differed concerning this reference.

Some said: it refers back to the blessings which Allah enumerated in these verses. Ikrimah said: A group from the people of Yemen came to Ibn Abbas, and a man asked him about this verse. He said: "Recite what precedes it: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships...﴾ up to Allah's words ﴿a way﴾." Ibn Abbas then said: "Whoever was blind in these blessings which he saw and witnessed, is blind regarding the matter of the Hereafter, which he did not see nor witness, ﴿blind and further astray from the way﴾."

Others said: it refers back to this world. The meaning is: whoever was blind in this world to the power of Allah and His signs, will be blind in the Hereafter.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: whoever was blind in this world to His proof, will be blind in the Hereafter to His Paradise.

Al-Hasan said: whoever was astray and a disbeliever in this world, will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray, because he did not repent in this world, and in the Hereafter his repentance will not be accepted.

The readers differed concerning these two words (a'mā). The people of Kufa pronounced them with imalah (inclination), while the others pronounced them with fakhm (emphatic, full vowel).

As for Abu Amr, he would pronounce the first with kasrah and the second with fath, meaning: "in the Hereafter he is more blind," on the basis of His saying ﴿and further astray﴾. This is the choice of Abu Ubaydah.

Al-Farra' said: a shaykh from the people of Basra related to me in Syria that he heard from the Arabs saying: "How black his hair is (ma aswad sha'rahu)."

The poet said:
"As for the kings, today you are the nations in baseness, and the whitest of them is a cook's garment." [[Lisan al-Arab: 7/124, and al-Mustadrak: 4/551.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 60–72 (part 1 of 2):

And [mention] when We said to you, "Indeed your Lord has encompassed the people." They are within His grip; they cannot escape His will. He is your protector against them and your guardian, so do not fear them, and carry out what He has commanded you in conveying His message. This is the view of most of the exegetes.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that His knowledge encompasses them, so nothing of them is hidden from Him.

Muqatil and al-Bara' said: "encompassed the people" means the people of Makkah, i.e., that it (Makkah) will be opened for you.

﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾.

Some people said: it is a visual vision, namely what the Prophet ﷺ was shown on the night of the Mi'raj of wonders and signs, and that was a trial for the people: some denied and called it a lie, some apostatized, and some affirmed it. The Arabs say: "I saw with my eye" (ra'aytu bi-'ayni) "ru'yah" and "ru'ya." On this basis is to be understood the hadith of Mu'awiyah that when he was asked about the Night Journey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "It was a true vision from Allah," i.e., a vision seen with the eyes, which Allah showed to His Prophet ﷺ. And what we have mentioned as the interpretation of the verse is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Masruq, Abu Malik, Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jurayj, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, and 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

Others said: it is what Allah showed His Prophet ﷺ on the night he was taken by night in his spirit without his body. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ related it to his companions [.........] [[an unreadable word.]] from among the companions of the Muslims, and some of the hypocrites criticized it. And this is what

Jarir ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who related from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the morning prayer, he would face the people with his face and say: "Did any of you see a dream last night?" If anyone had seen a dream that night, he would relate it to him, and he would say about it whatever Allah willed him to say. One day he asked us: "Did any of you see a dream last night?" We said: "No." He said: "But I was visited last night by two visitors who said to me: 'Come along.' So I went with them, and they took me to a level land, and there was a man lying on his back, and another man standing over him with a rock in his hand, smashing his head with it. [Then the rock rolls away], and when he goes to take it, the head returns as it was, and he does the same to him again." I said: "What is this?"

They said: "Come along." So I went with them and came to a man lying on his back, and another standing over him with an iron hook, who seized one side of his face and tore his cheek to his nape, his eye to his nape, and his nostril to his nape; then he turns to the other side and does the same to it. He does not finish until that side returns as it was, and then he returns to it." I said to them: "Glory be to God, what is this?" They said: "Come along." So I went with them and came to a building shaped like an oven, narrow at the top and wide at the bottom, in which a fire was kindled. We looked into it and there were men and women, naked, and flames came to them from below; when the flames reached them from below, they cried out. I said: "Who are these?"

They said: "Come along." So we went and came to a river of red blood, and in it a swimmer swimming, and on the bank of the river a man with many stones before him. The swimmer comes to the one who has gathered the stones before him, and he opens his mouth, and he puts a stone in it; then he goes off swimming, and then returns to him, and he opens his mouth [sic, as in the original] and he puts a stone in it. I said: "What is this?" They said: "Come along." So I went and came to a man of the most hideous appearance, the ugliest man I have ever seen, and beside him was a fire, which he was stoking and running around it. I said to them: "What is this?" They said: "Come along." So we went and came to a verdant garden [thick with growth], containing every kind of spring flower, and there was a great tree, and at its root an elderly tall man, and around him children, more than I have ever seen. I said: "Who are these?" They said: "Come along." So we went and came to a great tree, larger than any tree I have ever seen, and [no more beautiful]. They said to me: "Ascend," so we ascended and reached a city built of gold and silver bricks. We came to the gate of the city and asked for it to be opened, and it was opened for us, and we entered. There we were met by men, half of whose creation was [as beautiful as] the most beautiful I have seen, and half [as ugly as] the ugliest I have seen. They said to them: "Go and plunge into that river," and there was a river flowing across, as if it were churned milk for its whiteness. They went and plunged into it, then returned to us, and the evil had left them, and they became in the best form. He said: I said to them, "By God, I have never seen anything as wondrous as tonight; what is this that I have seen?" They said: "We will inform you. As for the one whose head you saw being smashed with the rock, he is a man who takes the Qur'an and rejects it and sleeps through the obligatory prayer. As for the one whose cheek, eye and nostril you saw being torn to his nape, he is a man [who goes out] from his house and tells a lie that reaches the horizons [the lie spreads to every region]." [[supplied from al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

As for the naked men and women in the oven-like building, they are the fornicators, male and female. As for the man swimming in the river and swallowing stones, he is the consumer of usury. As for the hideous man beside the fire that he stokes, he is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. As for the tall man in the [garden], he is Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and as for the children around him, every child is born upon the fitrah.

As for the people who were half beautiful and half ugly, they are people who "mixed a righteous deed with another evil," so Allah pardoned them. As for the garden, it is "Gardens of Eden," and as for the city I entered, it is the abode of the martyrs.

He said: "While my gaze was rising, there was something like a white fly." They said to me: "This is your abode." I am Jibril, and this is Mika'il. I said: "May Allah bless you both; let me enter my abode." They said: "There remains for you something you have not completed; had you completed it, you would have entered your abode." [37] [[in full in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur 3/274, with slight variation.]]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It is the vision in which he saw that he and his companions would enter Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, while he was in Madinah at that time. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hastened toward Makkah before the appointed time, but the polytheists turned him back.

Some people said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it." So his return became a trial for them. Then in the following year the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for it and entered it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Hudhayfah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, on the saying of Allah, ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾, said: He saw the Banu Umayyah on the pulpits, and that distressed him. It was said to him: "It is only the world, which they are given, [and it is withheld] from him." ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾: a test for the people.

Abd al-Muhaymin narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the Banu Umayyah leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that distressed him, so he was never seen laughing until he died. Thereupon Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the cursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an﴾, meaning the tree of Zaqqum.

The meaning of the verse: "the cursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an" is connected by "al-shajarah" being conjoined to "al-ru'ya." Its interpretation: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you, and the cursed tree in the Qur'an, except as a trial for the people." So their trial in the vision was what has been mentioned, and their trial in the cursed tree was that when this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said: "Is it not a lie that Ibn Abi Kabshah threatens you with burning by stones, then claims that a tree will grow in it, though you know that fire burns trees? So what do they say about the Zaqqum?"

'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari [sic, as in the original] said: "It is butter and dates in the Berber language."

Abu Jahl said: "O slave girl, bring us zaqqum." She brought him butter and dates. He said: "O people, this is what Muhammad frightens you with; by God, Zaqqum is only known as butter and dates." Then Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is the food of the sinful﴾ [[Surah al-Dukhan: 43, 44.]] and described it in al-Saffat: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire﴾ [[Surah al-Saffat: 64.]], meaning that it was created from fire and fashioned from it. And Allah revealed: ﴿And We warn them, but it increases them only in great transgression﴾.

Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from a client of the Banu Hashim who told him that 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal [sent] [[as in the original.]] to Ibn 'Abbas: "Are we the cursed tree in the Qur'an?" He said: He said: "The cursed tree is this tree that twines around trees," meaning the dodder (kushuth). [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/286.]]

﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He said: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ meaning from clay.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Lord of Might sent Iblis, and he took a handful of the surface of the earth, of its sweet and salty parts, and from it created Adam. So everything He created from its sweet part is destined for happiness even if it is the son of two disbelievers, and everything He created from its salty part is destined for wretchedness even if it is the son of two prophets.

He said: For this reason Iblis said: "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?" meaning: "This clay—I brought it." For this reason Adam was named, because he was created from the surface of the earth. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/145.]]

He said: ﴿Iblis said: "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants,"﴾ i.e., I will surely take control of his offspring, gather them, and destroy them through misguidance, and utterly uproot them. It is said: "Fulan ihtanaka what Fulan has of knowledge or perfection," meaning he took it all, extracted and seized it entirely. And "the locust ihtanaka the crop" when it eats it all. The poet said:

"I complain to You of a year that has ravaged,
and has stripped our wealth and uprooted it."

It is also said that it is from the Arab saying: "hanaka al-dabbah yahnikuha" when one ties a rope under its lower jaw by which to lead it until it becomes steady.

﴿Except a few﴾, meaning the protected ones whom Allah excepted in His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 42.]]. He said: ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾, i.e., your recompense and the recompense of your followers, a complete reward. ﴿And incite﴾ [i.e., seize], ﴿entice, lead astray, and make them slide﴾ ﴿whomever you can among them﴾, i.e., among the offspring of Adam, ﴿with your voice﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "by your calling them to disobedience of Allah; every caller to disobedience is among the soldiers of Iblis."

Mujahid said: "by singing and musical instruments."

﴿And urge against them﴾, i.e., gather and shout. Muqatil: "entice them away from Him."

﴿with your horsemen and your footmen﴾, i.e., the riders of his army and his infantry.

The exegetes said: every rider and walker in disobedience to Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah: He has horsemen and footmen among the jinn and humans; whoever rides and fights in disobedience is from Iblis's horsemen, and whoever walks and fights in disobedience to Allah is from Iblis's footmen. "Rajil" means infantry.

Hafs recited "wa-rajilika" with a kasrah on the ra', and both are dialects: "rajil" and "rajil," like "tajir" and "tajir," and "rakib" and "rakib."

﴿And share with them in wealth﴾. Some people said: it is every wealth acquired unlawfully and spent unlawfully. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: it is usury. Qatadah: what the polytheists used to forbid of livestock, such as the bahair, the sawaib, the wasilah, and the hawami; this is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Dahhak said: it is what they used to slaughter for their gods.

﴿And the children.﴾

Some said: they are children of fornication. This is the view of Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and the narration of 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Walibi from him: it is what they accepted from their children and committed unlawful acts with regard to them.

al-Hasan and Qatadah: the enemy of Allah shared with them in their wealth and children, so they were made Magians, Jews, and Christians, and dyed with other than the dye of Islam. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/152.]]

Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: his sharing with them in the children is in naming them their children: 'Abd al-Harith, 'Abd Shams, and 'Abd Fulan.

﴿And promise them﴾, and give them false hopes of obedience to you. Allah says: ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾, i.e., falsehood and deception, because he cannot avail them against the punishment of Allah when it descends upon them, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 22.]].

﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them; and sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs.﴾ ﴿Your Lord is He who drives [ships] for you [smoothly and makes them run]﴾ ﴿in the sea, to the saying: "and when harm touches you at sea"﴾, i.e., hardship befalls you [at sea], and you fear drowning, ﴿those you invoke vanish except Him﴾, i.e., except your supplication to Him, and you find nothing that suffices you other than Him. ﴿But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away﴾ from faith and obedience and disbelieve in what has come to you. ﴿And man has always been ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the earth to swallow you at the side of the land, or send against you a sandstorm﴾, i.e., He will make you disappear and perish; or send against you a hasib: stones raining down upon you from the sky, as He rained upon the people of Lot.

Abu 'Ubayd and al-Qutaybi said: the hasib is that which pelts with pebbles, which are small stones.

al-Farazdaq said:
"Facing the north of Syria, it strikes us
with a hasib like scattered cotton fluff."

﴿Then you will not find for yourselves any protector. Or do you feel secure that He will return you into it [the sea] another time, and send against you a violent wind and drown you for your disbelief? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger.﴾ Qatadah: "qasifan" means a violent wind; Ibn 'Abbas and Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is that which shatters everything, i.e., crushes and breaks it, and it is what breaks trees.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "nakhsifa, nursila, nu'idukum, and nughriqakum" all with nun, because of His saying "'alayna" (against Us). The rest recited them all with ya', because of His saying "iyyah" (Him). Except Abu Ja'far, who recited "tughriqakum" with ta', meaning the wind.

﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam.﴾ Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam," said: every creature eats with its mouth except the son of Adam, who eats with his hands; and also from him: with intellect.

al-Dahhak: with speech and discernment.

'Ata': the balance and proportion of the general form and its extension. Yaman: with beauty of form.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: in that He made Muhammad among them. It is also said: men with beards and women with forelocks.

Muhammad ibn Jarir: in His giving them power over other creatures and subjecting all creatures to them.

﴿And We carried them on land and sea and provided for them of the good things﴾, meaning delicious foods and drinks.

Muqatil: ghee, butter, dates, and sweets, and the provision of others is what is hidden from you.

﴿And We preferred them over much of what We have created, with [marked] preference.﴾

Some people said: His saying "much of what We have created" is an exception for the angels.

al-Kalbi said: they are preferred over all creatures except a group of angels: Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and their like.

Others said: what is meant is all of what We have created; the Arabs sometimes place "the greater" and "the many" in the position of the plural and the whole, as in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar. They listen eagerly, and most of them are liars﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara: 222–223]], and what is meant is all the devils.

Ma'mar from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam," said: the angels said: "Our Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world to eat and enjoy in it, and You did not give us that; so give us the Hereafter." He said: "By My might and My majesty, I will not make the offspring of those whom I created with My hand like what I said to them: 'Be,' and it is."

Hammad ibn Salamah from Abu al-Mahram, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: "The believer is more honored by Allah than the angels who are with Him."

﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: with their prophet. What supports this is what al-Suddi narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying, "The Day We will call every people with their leader": he said, with their prophet.

Abu Salih, Abu Nadr, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: with their book which was revealed to them, and it is

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 60–72 (part 2 of 2):

The narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, and from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Murtada (peace be upon them), from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning "the Day We shall call every people with their imam": "Every people will be brought with the imam of their time, the Book of their Lord, and the Sunnah of their Prophet" [38].

Abu al-Aliyah and al-Hasan said: "with their deeds." The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, in the context of the verse, ﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record﴾, and its parallel, His saying ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register (imam mubin)﴾. Thus the Book is called an imam.

Ibn Shihab narrated from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever spends a pair [of things] in the cause of Allah will be called from the Gardens: 'O servant of Allah, this is good.' Whoever was among the people of prayer will be called from the Gate of Prayer; whoever was among the people of jihad will be called from the Gate of Jihad; whoever was among the people of charity will be called from the Gate of Charity; and whoever was among the people of fasting will be called from the Gate of al-Rayyan."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, there is no necessity for one called from those gates; but will anyone be called from all of them?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them" [39] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/227, and Sahih Muslim: 3/91.]].

The hadith of the banners and standards also confirms this statement.

Badhan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas: "with their imam" means the one who called them in this world to misguidance or to guidance.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah: "with their leaders in good and evil."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them imams calling to the Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 41.]], and it was said: "with their worshipped ones."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "with their mothers."

The wise have said: in this there are three aspects of wisdom. The first: for the sake of Isa (peace be upon him). The second: to honour the noble lineage of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). The third: so that the children of fornication are not exposed.

Regarding ﴿Whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾ up to His saying ﴿and whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind [in the Hereafter]﴾, the scholars differed concerning this reference.

Some said: it refers back to the blessings which Allah enumerated in these verses. Ikrimah said: A group from the people of Yemen came to Ibn Abbas, and a man asked him about this verse. He said: "Recite what precedes it: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships...﴾ up to Allah's words ﴿a way﴾." Ibn Abbas then said: "Whoever was blind in these blessings which he saw and witnessed, is blind regarding the matter of the Hereafter, which he did not see nor witness, ﴿blind and further astray from the way﴾."

Others said: it refers back to this world. The meaning is: whoever was blind in this world to the power of Allah and His signs, will be blind in the Hereafter.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: whoever was blind in this world to His proof, will be blind in the Hereafter to His Paradise.

Al-Hasan said: whoever was astray and a disbeliever in this world, will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray, because he did not repent in this world, and in the Hereafter his repentance will not be accepted.

The readers differed concerning these two words (a'mā). The people of Kufa pronounced them with imalah (inclination), while the others pronounced them with fakhm (emphatic, full vowel).

As for Abu Amr, he would pronounce the first with kasrah and the second with fath, meaning: "in the Hereafter he is more blind," on the basis of His saying ﴿and further astray﴾. This is the choice of Abu Ubaydah.

Al-Farra' said: a shaykh from the people of Basra related to me in Syria that he heard from the Arabs saying: "How black his hair is (ma aswad sha'rahu)."

The poet said:
"As for the kings, today you are the nations in baseness, and the whitest of them is a cook's garment." [[Lisan al-Arab: 7/124, and al-Mustadrak: 4/551.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 17, verses 73–77:**

Concerning the verse, "And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you..." (The Qur'an, 17:73), the scholars differ regarding the occasion of its revelation.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to touch the Black Stone, and the Quraysh prevented him, saying: "We will not leave you alone until you touch our gods." He spoke to himself, saying: "What harm is there if I touch them, while God knows that I dislike it?" Then, after they had asked him to touch the Black Stone, God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Quraysh spoke with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) one night until the morning, speaking to him, offering him things, making him their leader, and bargaining with him. Among what they said was: "You bring something that no one among mankind has brought, and you are our master; so where is our master?" They kept speaking with him until he nearly inclined to them in some of what they wanted. Then God, exalted, protected him from that, and revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: They praised their gods and mentioned them, and they rejoiced. Ibn [Jumuh]: They came to him and said: "Go to our gods and touch them." This is His saying, "[you would have inclined to them] a little."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The delegation of Thaqif came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We will pledge allegiance to you on condition that you give us three things."

He said: "What are they?" They said: "We will not bow in prayer, we will not break our idols with our own hands, and [you will let us enjoy al-Lat] for a year."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them: "There is no good in a religion without bowing or prostration. As for not breaking your idols with your own hands, that is for you. As for the worship of al-Lat, I will not grant you enjoyment of it." [[Thus in the original.]] [40].

Then they said to the Messenger of God: "We wish that the Arabs would hear that you gave us what you did not give anyone else. If you dislike that, and fear that the Arabs would say, 'You gave them what you did not give us,' then say that God has commanded you to do so." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) remained silent and invited them to believe. 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) understood that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had been asked, and said: "What is wrong with you? You have harmed the Messenger of God (ﷺ)! May God burn your livers! The Messenger of God will not leave idols in the land of the Arabs. Either you embrace Islam, or you return; we have no need of you." [[Ta'rikh al-Madina of Ibn Shabbah: 2/511, and al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Kathir: 4/56.]].

Then God, exalted, revealed this verse, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) promised to give them that.

'Atiyyah, on his authority, said: Thaqif said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Grant us a year until we collect what is offered to our gods. When we have collected what is offered to our gods, we will break them and embrace Islam." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved to grant them a delay, so God, exalted, revealed: "And indeed they almost tempted you" (wa-in kadu la-yaftinunaka), and they had resolved, "to make you slip" (liyastazilunaka) and "to turn you away from that which We revealed to you" (ʿan alladhi awhayna ilayka), "to invent against Us other than it" (li-taftariya), that is, to differ with Us about it; "and then they would have taken you as a friend" (wa-idhan la-ittakhadhuka khalilan), that is, they would have loved you and become close to you.

"And had We not made you firm" (wa-law la an thabbatnaka), upon the truth by Our help, "you would almost have inclined toward them a little" (la-qad kidta tarkanu ilayhim shay'an qalilan). And had you done that, "then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double in death" (idhan la-adhaqnaka ḍiʿfa al-ḥayati wa-ḍiʿfa al-mamati), the mahdar (the dying), that is, double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning We would have doubled the punishment for you in this world and the Hereafter. "Then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us" (thumma la tajidu laka ʿalayna naṣiran), one who would protect you from Our punishment.

Qatadah said: When these verses were revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O God, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye." [41].

Concerning the verse, "And indeed they almost drove you out of the land (wa-in kadu la-yastafizzunaka min al-ard) to expel you from it..."

al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Medina, the Jews envied his residence in Medina and disliked his closeness to them. They came and said: "O Muhammad, are you a prophet?" He said: "Yes." They said: "By God, you know that this is not the land of the prophets; the land of the prophets is Syria, and I see Abraham and [the prophets] there. If you are a prophet like them, go to Syria; we know that what prevents you from going there is your fear of the Romans, and that God will protect you there from the Romans if you are His messenger. It is the Holy Land, and prophets do not appear in this city."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) encamped at a distance of three or four miles from Medina, and in some reports up to Dhu al-Hulayfah, until he could scout and his companions could gather around him and the people could see him. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And indeed they almost drove you out of the land" (wa-in kadu la-yastafizzunaka min al-ard), the land in which you were, which is the land of Medina. [[This is among the clearest of fabrications, that the Supreme Messenger would abandon revelation and take from the Jews. An ordinary, naive person would not accept this statement, so how much less the Prophet of Guidance, who does not speak from desire, who is the most intelligent of the Arabs and their chief, and who is protected from error, as the Islamic sects have unanimously agreed and as is established in its proper place.]].

Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam: The Jews came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, if you are truthful that you are a prophet, then go to Syria, for it is the land of the gathering and resurrection and the land of the prophets." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) accepted what they said, and in the expedition of Tabuk he intended nothing but Syria. When he reached Tabuk, God revealed to him a verse from Surat Bani Isra'il after which the surah ends: "And indeed they almost drove you out of the land..." (the verse), and He commanded him to return to Medina, saying: "In it are your cavalry and your kingdom, and in it is your mission."

Mujahid and Qatadah said: The people of Mecca resolved deliberately to expel the Prophet (ﷺ) from Mecca. Had they done so, they would not have settled there; but God restrained them from expelling him until He commanded him to leave. Yet they would have remained only a little while after the Prophet's departure from Mecca before God destroyed them on the Day of Badr. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/166.]].

This interpretation is more fitting to the verse, because what precedes it concerns the people of Mecca, and no mention of the Jews is made; and because this surah is Meccan.

It was also said: They are all the disbelievers, who almost drove him out of the land of the Arabs through their gathering and their combined support against him. But God protected His Messenger (ﷺ), and they did not attain from him what they hoped of victory. Had they expelled him from the land of the Arabs, they would not have stayed there in their disbelief, but would have been destroyed by punishment. This is His saying: "And indeed they almost drove you out of the land to expel you from it; then they would not have remained after you [khalfaka]," that is, after you. This is the reading of Abu 'Amr and the people of the Hijaz, and it was chosen by Abu 'Ubayd.

The rest read khilafaka, and Abu Hatim chose it, considering His saying: "Those who remained behind rejoiced in their sitting [behind] in opposition [khilafa] to the Messenger of God" [[Surat al-Tawbah: 81.]], and its meaning is also "after you."

The poet said:

"The dwellings were effaced after her [khilafaha], as if the palm-fibre weavers had spread a mat of them."

That is, after her.

"Except a little" (illa qalilan): until you perish. "The way of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers" (sunnata man qad arsalna qablaka min rusulina), that is, as is Our custom with those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: when their peoples denied them, We destroyed them with punishment; and We did not punish them as long as their prophet was among them. But when their prophet left them, We punished them. "And you will not find any alteration in Our custom" (wa-la tajidu li-sunnatina tahwilan), that is, any change.

Yet they would have remained only a little while after the Prophet's departure from Mecca before God destroyed them on the Day of Badr. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/166.]].

This interpretation is more fitting to the verse, because what precedes it concerns the people of Mecca, and no mention of the Jews is made; and because this surah is Meccan.

It was also said: They are all the disbelievers, who almost drove him out of the land of the Arabs through their gathering and their combined support against him. But God protected His Messenger (ﷺ), and they did not attain from him what they hoped of victory. Had they expelled him from the land of the Arabs, they would not have stayed there in their disbelief, but would have been destroyed by punishment. This is His saying: "And indeed they almost drove you out of the land to expel you from it; then they would not have remained after you [khalfaka]," that is, after you. This is the reading of Abu 'Amr and the people of the Hijaz, and it was chosen by Abu 'Ubayd.

The rest read khilafaka, and Abu Hatim chose it, considering His saying: "Those who remained behind rejoiced in their sitting [behind] in opposition [khilafa] to the Messenger of God" [[Surat al-Tawbah: 81.]], and its meaning is also "after you."

The poet said:

"The dwellings were effaced after her [khilafaha], as if the palm-fibre weavers had spread a mat of them."

That is, after her.

"Except a little" (illa qalilan): until you perish. "The way of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers" (sunnata man qad arsalna qablaka min rusulina), that is, as is Our custom with those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: when their peoples denied them, We destroyed them with punishment; and We did not punish them as long as their prophet was among them. But when their prophet left them, We punished them. "And you will not find any alteration in Our custom" (wa-la tajidu li-sunnatina tahwilan), that is, any change.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 78–84 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi, Yaman and Ibn Zayd said: its "dulūk" (decline) is its setting.

The poet said:
"This is the station of my feet, Riyah... from dawn until Barah was destroyed."
That is, the sun set, and Barah is a name for the sun, like Qatam, Judham and Rafash.

It is also related as "Barāh" with a kasra on the ba', meaning that the observer places his palm over his brow because of the glare of its rays, in order to see what remains of its dust, and this is said of the sun when it has set.

Dhu al-Rummah said:
"Lamps not like those led by them... stars, not like the wandering ones that dwell (?)"

The evidence for this interpretation is the report of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that when the sun set he would pray Maghrib and break his fast if he was fasting, and he would swear by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the appointed time for this prayer, and it is what Allah meant by ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.

Ibn 'Umrah, Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ata', Qatadah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Muqatil, Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Ubayd ibn Hajar said: its "dulūk" is its declining (after midday), and al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said likewise. What supports this is the report of Abu Mas'ud 'Uqbah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril came to me at the decline of the sun, when the sun had passed its zenith, and led me in the Zuhr prayer." [42] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/171.]]

Abu Barzah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pray Zuhr when the sun had passed its zenith, then he recited this verse: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I invited the Prophet (ﷺ) and whoever of his companions wished, and they ate at my place, then they went out when the sun had passed its zenith. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out and said: "Go out, Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined."

On this interpretation, the verse comprises all the times of prayer: "the decline of the sun" is the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, and "the darkness of the night" is the two 'Isha' prayers. The confirmation of this explanation is that Jibril (peace be upon him), when he taught the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the manner of prayer, began with the Zuhr prayer.

Muhammad ibn 'Ammar related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril came to me and prayed Zuhr with me when the sun had declined. Then he came to me and prayed 'Asr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to it. Then he prayed Maghrib with me when the sun had set. Then he prayed 'Isha' with me when the twilight had disappeared. Then he came to me and prayed Subh with me when the dawn had broken. Then he came to me the next day and prayed Zuhr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to it, then he prayed 'Asr with me when the shadow of everything was twice its length, then he prayed Maghrib with me when the sun had set, then he prayed 'Isha' with me when a third of the night had passed, then he prayed Subh with me when it had become bright. Then he said: 'These are the prayers of the prophets before you, so keep to them.'" [43] [[Al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 1/532, no. 2029.]]

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah related from Jabir, who said: Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to teach him the times of prayer. Jibril went forward while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was behind him and the people were behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed Zuhr when the sun had passed its zenith. Then he came to him when the shadow was equal to a person's height, and did as he had done, and Jibril went forward with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed 'Asr.

Then he came to him when the sun had set, and he prayed Maghrib, with Jibril having gone forward and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed Maghrib. Then he came to him when the twilight had disappeared, and Jibril went forward with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed 'Isha'. Then Jibril came to him when the dawn had broken, and Jibril went forward with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) behind him and the people behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he prayed the morning prayer. Then he came to him on the second day when the shadow of a man was equal to his height, and he did as he had done the day before, and he prayed Zuhr. Then he came to him when the shadow of a man among us was equal to his two heights, and he did as he had done the day before, and he prayed 'Asr. Then he came to him when the sun had set, and he did as he had done the day before, and he prayed Maghrib at the same time as before. Then he came to him and did as he had done the day before, and he prayed 'Isha'.

Then he began the dawn prayer and it was morning while the stars were visible and interlaced, and he did as he had done the day before and prayed the morning prayer. Then he said: "Between these two prayers is the time."

And from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril came to me twice at the door of the Ka'bah. He prayed Zuhr when the shadow was like the strap of a sandal. Then he prayed 'Asr when everything was equal to its shadow. Then he prayed Maghrib when the fasting person breaks his fast. Then he prayed 'Isha' when the twilight had disappeared. Then he prayed Subh when food and drink became forbidden to the fasting person. Then he prayed Zuhr on the last occasion when everything was equal to its shadow, at the time of 'Asr the day before. Then he prayed 'Asr when the shadow of a thing was twice its length. Then he prayed Maghrib at its first time, not delaying it. Then he prayed the last 'Isha' when a third of the night had passed. Then he prayed Subh when it was bright. Then he turned and said: 'O Muhammad, this is the time of the prophets before you; the time lies between these two times.'" [44] [[Ibid., no. 2028.]]

﴿Until the darkness of the night﴾: its coming with its darkness.
Ibn 'Abbas said: the beginning of the night. Qatadah: the Maghrib prayer.
Mujahid: the setting of the sun. Abu 'Ubaydah: its blackness.
Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat:
"Indeed this night has grown dark, so I complained of worry and sleeplessness." [[Lisan al-'Arab: 10/288.]]
It is also said: ghasaqa yaghsiqu ghusuqan. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/304.]]

﴿And the recitation of dawn﴾: that is, the dawn prayer. It is called "recitation" because it is not valid without recitation. It is also said: it means what is recited in the dawn prayer.

The accusative of "al-Qur'an" has two aspects. One: it is conjoined to "the prayer", meaning "establish the recitation of dawn", as al-Farra' said. The People of Basra said: it is in the sense of an incitement (al-ighra'), meaning "and keep to the recitation of dawn".

Some of them said: its gathering and its clarity; in that case the meaning is "establish prayer at the decline of the sun" together with the recitation of dawn.

﴿Indeed the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾: the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it. These descend and those ascend, so it is at the end of the night's record and the beginning of the day's record. In this verse there is clear evidence that the obligation of prayer is tied to the beginning of its time, and that it is recommended to pray the dawn prayer in the dark (al-taghlis).

Al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The merit of a congregational prayer over a single prayer is twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Subh prayer." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/553, no. 20218; and Musnad Ahmad: 2/266.]]

He said: Abu Hurayrah would say: Recite, if you wish: ﴿And the recitation of dawn; indeed the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾.

﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it﴾: that is, rise after your sleep and pray.

The exegetes said: tahajjud is only after sleep. It is said: "tahajjada" if he stayed awake, and "hajada" if he slept. [[Al-Hujud is sleep from it.]]

Some people of the language said: it is said "tahajjada" for sleeping and "tahajjada" for staying awake, and it is among the words with opposite meanings (al-adhdad).

Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf related from a man of the Ansar that he was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey and said: "I will surely watch how the Prophet (ﷺ) prays." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept, then woke up, raised his head to the sky and recited four verses from Surah Al 'Imran: ﴿Indeed in the creation of the heavens and the earth... are signs﴾. Then he reached his hand to the water-skin, took a siwak and cleaned his teeth with it, then performed ablution, then prayed, then slept, then woke up, and did as he had done the first time. They claim that this is the tahajjud which Allah the Exalted commanded.
[[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/84, no. 10139.]]

﴿A supererogatory (nafilah) for you﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: specially for you. Muqatil ibn Hayyan: an honour and a gift for you.

Ibn 'Abbas: your obligation.

He said: the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to stand in the night specifically, and it was prescribed for him, so the meaning of "nafilah" on this view is an obligation that Allah imposed on you, in addition to the obligations that He imposed on us, as an increase.

Qatadah said: voluntary and as a virtue. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/179.]]

Some scholars said: the night prayer was obligatory for him at the beginning, then he was permitted to leave it, so it became supererogatory. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/309.]]

Mujahid said: the nafilah is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), because Allah forgave him what came before of his sin and what came after; so whatever deed he does beyond the obligatory prayers is a supererogatory for him, since he does not do it as expiation for sins as others do. For them, the supererogatory prayers beyond the obligatory ones are for expiation of their sins, so they are not supererogatory for people.

﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾.

The people of interpretation said: "'asā" (it may be) and "la'alla" (perhaps), when from Allah, are an assurance, because He does not fail to do for His servants what He has given them hope of as reward for their obedience, since it is not His attribute to deceive. Were a man to say to another: "Guide me and stay with me, perhaps I will benefit you," and then he stayed with him and did not benefit him despite having given him hope and promise, it would be a disgrace to him, and Allah is exalted above that. As for the praiseworthy station, it is the station in which he intercedes for his community, and the first and the last will praise him in it.

'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had I taken a close friend, I would have taken Ibn Abi Quhafah as a close friend; but your companion is the friend of Allah." Then he recited: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾. [45] [['Ilal al-Daraqutni: 5/320; and Da'if Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 490, no. 753.]]

And from Huthayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: People will be gathered in one level plain, and no soul will speak, and he will be the first to call upon Muhammad (ﷺ), who will say: "Here I am at your service and bidding, good is in Your hands, evil is not attributed to You, the guided is the one You guided, Your servant is before You, by You and to You; there is no refuge nor escape from You except to You. Blessed are You and exalted, glory be to You, Lord of the House." That is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾.

Qatadah, from Ma'mun ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be inspired, saying: 'If only we sought intercession with our Lord, so that He would relieve us from this place.' So they will come to Adam (peace be upon him) and say: 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind; Allah created you with His hand, made His angels prostrate to you, and taught you the names of everything; so intercede for us with your Lord, that He may relieve us from this place.' He will say to them: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention the sin he committed, and he will be ashamed before his Lord because of it. But go to Nuh, for he is the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth. They will come to Nuh, and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention his error and his asking his Lord for the destruction of his people, and he will be ashamed. But go to Ibrahim, the friend of the Merciful. They will come to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and he will say: 'I am not fit for that; but go to Musa, a servant whom Allah spoke to and to whom He gave the Torah.' They will come to Musa (peace be upon him), and he will say: 'I am not fit for that,' and he will mention to them the soul he killed without a soul, and he will be ashamed of that. He will say: 'Go to 'Isa, the servant of Allah and His messenger, the word of Allah and His spirit.' They will come to 'Isa (peace be upon him), and he will say: 'I am not fit for that; but go to Muhammad, a servant whose previous and later sins Allah has forgiven.' They will come to me, and I will rise and walk between two rows of believers until I ask permission of my Lord, and it will be granted to me. When I see my Lord, I will fall down prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me for as long as He wills. Then He will say: 'Raise your head; speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.' I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise He will teach me, and then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return to Him a second time, and when I see my Lord I will fall down, or prostrate, to my Lord, and He will leave me for as long as He wills. Then He will say: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted.' I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise, and then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return to Him a third time, and when I see my Lord I will fall down prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me for as long as He wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak, and you will be heard; ask, and you will be given; intercede,' and I will intercede, and I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise He will teach me, and then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return to Him a fourth time, and I will say: 'O Lord, there remains only the one whom the Qur'an has held back.'"

Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' and has in his heart goodness equal to the weight of a barley grain will be brought out of the Fire; then whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' and has in his heart goodness equal to the weight of an atom will be brought out of the Fire." [46] [[In full in Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/60.]]

Abu 'Asim Muhammad ibn Abi Ayyub al-Thaqafi related from Yazid ibn Suhayb, who said: I had been preoccupied by the opinion of those who hold the views of the Kharijites, and I was a young man. He said: We set out in a band of a number, intending to perform Hajj and then rise against the people. We passed by Madinah, and there was Jabir ibn Abdullah relating to the people from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sitting by a pillar, and he mentioned the people of Hell. I said to him: "O companion of the Messenger of Allah, what is this you relate, when Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Indeed whomever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him, and whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned into it﴾?"

He said to me: "Do you recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you heard of the praiseworthy station of Muhammad (ﷺ) in which Allah will raise him?" I said: "Yes." He said: "It is the praiseworthy station of Muhammad (ﷺ), by which Allah will bring out whomever He brings out of the Fire." [[Up to here in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/198.]]

Then he described the placing of the Sirat and the passage of people over it. He said: "I fear I have not memorised all of that, except that it is claimed that a people will come out of the Fire after having been in it. They will come out like the stalks of sesame, and they will enter a river of the rivers of Paradise and bathe in it, and they will come out like sheets of paper." He said: So we returned and said: "Do you see that this old man lies upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" By Allah, not one of us came out (of the rebellion) except one man.

Al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn Husayn, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a leather hide [of 'Ukazi], until no one among mankind has anything but the place of his feet." [47]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will be the first to be called, and Jibril will be on the right of the Merciful. By Allah, he had not seen him before that. I will say: 'O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me.' Allah the Exalted will say: 'He has spoken the truth.' Then I will intercede and say: 'O Lord, Your servants worshipped You in the far parts of the earth.'" He said: "That is the praiseworthy station." [48] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/183.]]

Sufyan related from Salamah ibn Suhayl, from Abu al-Za'ra', who said: 'Abdullah said: The first intercessor on the Day of Resurrection will be the Spirit of Holiness, Jibril, then Ibrahim, then Musa, then 'Isa, then your Prophet (ﷺ) will stand fourth, and no one will intercede after him in what he intercedes for; and that is the praiseworthy station. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/180.]]

Sa'id ibn 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Concerning al-Buraq: he said to Jibril, 'By Him who sent you with the truth, it will not carry me until it has guaranteed me the intercession.'"

Abdullah ibn Idris, from Abdullah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾. He said: "He will bring me near and seat me with Him upon the Throne."
Ibn Fanjawayh said: "He will seat me with Him upon His throne."

Abu Usamah, from Dawud ibn Yazid [al-Azdi], from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, said: "It is the intercession." [49]

'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: Allah the Exalted took Ibrahim as a friend, and your companion is the friend of Allah and the most honoured of creation before Allah; then he recited: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, and said: "He will seat him upon the Throne."

Sa'id al-Jarwi related from Sayf al-Sadusi, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, your Prophet (ﷺ) will be brought and seated before the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, upon the Kursi.

Layth related from Mujahid regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, he said: "He will seat him upon the Throne."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 17, verse 78–84 (part 2 of 2):

The Ustadh al-Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Tha'alibi said: This interpretation is not impossible, because God, before creating things, was self-subsisting (qa'iman bi-dhatihi). Then He created things without needing them, rather to manifest His power and wisdom, so that His existence alone would be known, along with the perfection of His knowledge and power through the manifestation of His acts, which are perfected by wisdom. He created for Himself a throne upon which He istawa (established Himself) as He wills, without that becoming something that came to Him by His will, nor was the throne a place for Him. Rather He is now in the same attribute He was in before He created place and time. According to this view, it makes no difference whether Muhammad ﷺ was seated upon the Throne or upon the earth, because God's istiwa' over the Throne does not mean approaching and receding, nor a change of states from standing to sitting, nor a condition that occupies the Throne. Rather He is established upon His Throne as He informed us about Himself, without asking how. Seating Muhammad ﷺ upon the Throne does not make him possess the attribute of lordship (rububiyyah), nor remove him from the attribute of servanthood ('ubudiyyah). Rather it is an elevation of his station, a manifestation of his nobility, and his being preferred over others of God's creation. As for their saying "with Him" in reports, it is like the words of God ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ and ﴿My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise﴾ and similar verses. All of that refers to rank and status, not to place and direction, and God knows best.

﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit."﴾ The common readers recited it with a dammah on both mim letters, meaning causing to enter and causing to exit.
Al-Hasan recited it with a fathah on both, meaning entering and exiting.
The exegetes differed in its interpretation.
Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ is Medina, and ﴿cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ is Mecca. It was revealed when the Messenger of God ﷺ was commanded to emigrate (hijrah).
Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When he entered the cave, ﴿My Lord, cause me to enter﴾, meaning the cave, ﴿a sound entrance, and cause me to exit﴾ from the cave ﴿a sound exit﴾ to Medina." [50] [[Tafsir Abi Hamzah al-Thumali: 237, no. 187, from al-Tha'alibi.]]
Al-Dahhak said: ﴿cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ from Mecca, safe from the polytheists; ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ into Mecca, dominant over it by conquest.
'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ is the grave at death, and ﴿cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ is from the grave at resurrection.
Al-Kalbi: ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ is Medina, when he entered it after having intended Syria; ﴿cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ from it to Mecca, open it for me.
Mujahid: ﴿cause me to enter﴾ into Your command with which You made me enter prophethood, ﴿a sound entrance﴾, and ﴿cause me to exit﴾ from it ﴿a sound exit﴾.
Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ into Your obedience, and ﴿cause me to exit a sound exit﴾, meaning safe, without falling short in it.
It was also said: its meaning is, cause me to enter wherever You cause me to enter with truthfulness, and cause me to exit with truthfulness, so that You make me among those who enter in one way and exit in one way, for the one of two faces is not trustworthy before God.

﴿And grant me from Yourself an authority, a helper.﴾ Mujahid: ﴿a clear proof﴾.
Al-Hasan said: meaning a strong kingdom through which He supports me against those who oppose me, and a manifest might by which I establish Your religion. He said:
So God promised him that He would surely strip the kingdom of Persia and Rome and their might, and He granted it to him.
Qatadah: The Prophet of God ﷺ knew that he had no capacity for this matter except with an authority, so he asked for ﴿an authority, a helper﴾ through the Book of God and its limits, its obligations, and the establishment of His religion. Indeed authority is a mercy from God, which He placed among His most manifest servants, so that none of them can overpower another, and the strong does not devour the weak.
It was also said: it is the conquest of Mecca.
Musa ibn Isma'il narrated from Hammad from al-Kalbi concerning ﴿grant me from Yourself an authority, a helper﴾, he said: His authority is the helper.
'Attab ibn Usayd ibn Abi al-'Is ibn Umayyah: The Messenger of God ﷺ appointed him over the people of Mecca [and said to him]: Go, for I have appointed you over the people of God, meaning Mecca. He was severe toward the [hypocrites] and gentle toward the believers.
He said: No, by God, I do not know of a latecomer who stays away from the prayer in congregation except that I would strike off his neck, for none stays away from it except a hypocrite.
The people of Mecca said: O Messenger of God, you appoint 'Attab ibn Usayd, a barefoot Bedouin, over the family of God?
The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I saw in a dream as one sees in sleep, as if 'Attab ibn Usayd came to the gate of Paradise and took hold of its ring and knocked on the door, not violently, until it was opened for him, and he entered it. So God made Islam mighty through him, by his support of the believers against those who wished to oppress them. That is the helping authority." [51] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/737, no. 33604, with variation.]]

﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished."﴾ That is, it came; ﴿and falsehood has vanished﴾, meaning the devil went away and was destroyed, said Qatadah.
Al-Suddi said: the truth is Islam and falsehood is polytheism. It was also said: the truth is the religion of the All-Merciful and falsehood is the idols.
Ibn Jurayj said: the truth is jihad and fighting.
﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾, meaning going away.
It is said: "his soul zahaqat" when it departed, and "the arrow zahaqa" when it passed the target and continued on its course.
Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ conquered Mecca, he found around the House three hundred and sixty idols, each people's idol in its place, and he had a staff. He would go to an idol and jab it in its eye or its belly, then say: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾, so the idol would fall on its face. The people of Mecca marveled and said among themselves: We have not seen a man more magical than Muhammad.
